title.zh: '''卷二百二十三上''' 列傳第一百四十八上 姦臣上

meta.sourceNote: Body created from Wikisource raw text because the ChineseNotes scrape produced a zero-byte file.

sentences.zh: ◎奸臣上許敬宗許敬宗，字延族，杭州新城人。

translations.literal: ◎ Corrupt Officials (Upper): Xu Jingzong. Xu Jingzong, courtesy name Yanzu, was a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Corrupt Officials (Upper) — Xu Jingzong. Xu Jingzong, whose courtesy name was Yanzu, came from Xincheng in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父善心，仕隋為給事中。

translations.literal: His father Shansin served the Sui as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shansin had served the Sui dynasty as a supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 敬宗幼善屬文，大業中舉秀才中第，調淮陽書佐，俄直謁者臺，奏通事舍人事。

translations.literal: Jingzong was skilled in literary composition from youth. In the Daye era he passed the xiucai examination, was assigned as secretary at Huaiyang, and soon served in the Office of Visitors, memorializing for appointment as Master of Ceremonial Intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Jingzong excelled at writing. During the Daye reign he passed the xiucai examination, was posted as a secretary at Huaiyang, and before long entered the Office of Visitors, where he petitioned for the post of master of ceremonial intercourse.

sentences.zh: 善心為宇文化及所殺，敬宗哀請得不死，去依李密為記室。

translations.literal: Shansin was killed by Yuwen Huaji. Jingzong pleaded piteously and was spared death. He left to serve Li Mi as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Shansin was killed by Yuwen Huaji, Jingzong begged so piteously that his life was spared. He then went over to Li Mi and served as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 武德初，補漣州別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era he was appointed Vice-Prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he was appointed vice-prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召署文學館學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard his name and summoned him to serve as a scholar of the Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of him, he summoned Jingzong to serve as a scholar in the Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，除著作郎，兼修國史，喜謂所親曰：「仕宦不為著作，無以成門戶。」

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he was appointed Director of Composition and concurrently compiled the national history. He said happily to those close to him: "In official service, if one is not a director of composition, one cannot establish a family line."
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he was made director of composition and also worked on the national history. He told his intimates with satisfaction, "In public life, unless you hold the post of director of composition you cannot build a lasting house for your family."

sentences.zh: 俄改中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon after he was changed to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the post of secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后喪，群臣衰服，率更令歐陽詢貌醜異，敬宗侮笑自如，貶洪州司馬。

translations.literal: At the mourning for Empress Wende, the ministers wore mourning garments. The Director of Palace Attendants Ouyang Xun had an ugly and strange appearance. Jingzong mocked and laughed as if at ease. He was demoted to military adjutant of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Empress Wende the court wore sackcloth, but when Ouyang Xun, director of palace attendants, appeared in his homely and odd looks, Jingzong openly mocked him. For this he was demoted to military adjutant of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 累轉給事中，復修史，以勞封高陽縣男，檢校黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Supervising Secretary, again compiled history, and for his labors was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang. He was made acting Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After further promotions to supervising secretary he again took up historical compilation and, for his service, was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang and made acting vice director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 高宗在東宮，遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Jingzong was moved to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong was still crown prince, Jingzong was appointed right vice director of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 高麗之役，太子監國定州，敬宗與高士廉典機劇。

translations.literal: During the campaign against Goguryeo, the crown prince supervised the state at Dingzhou. Jingzong and Gao Shilian managed urgent affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the war against Goguryeo the crown prince governed from Dingzhou, and Jingzong together with Gao Shilian handled the most pressing affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 岑文本卒，帝驛召敬宗，以本官檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Cen Wenti died, the emperor summoned Jingzong by post relay. With his existing office he was made acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Cen Wenti died the emperor summoned Jingzong by urgent relay and, while retaining his current rank, made him acting vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕山破賊，命草詔馬前，帝愛其藻警，由是專掌誥令。

translations.literal: At Zhujishan he defeated the rebels. The emperor ordered him to draft an edict before the horse. The emperor loved his polished and alert style. From this he exclusively managed imperial pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: When the army broke the rebels at Zhujishan, the emperor had him draft an edict from horseback and was so taken with his vivid, polished prose that Jingzong thereafter held sole charge of imperial edicts and commands.

sentences.zh: 初，太子承乾廢，官屬張玄素、令狐德棻、趙弘智、裴宣機、蕭鈞皆除名為民，不復用。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, his staff Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, and Xiao Jun were all struck from the rolls and made commoners, and were not employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, his staff members Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, and Xiao Jun were all stripped of office and reduced to commoners, never to be employed again.

sentences.zh: 敬宗為言玄素等以直言被嫌忌，今一概被罪，疑洗宥有所未至。

translations.literal: Jingzong spoke on behalf of Xuansu and the others, saying that because of their frank speech they had been resented, and that now to punish them all alike perhaps showed that pardon and leniency had not gone far enough.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong argued that Xuansu and the others had been resented precisely because they spoke plainly, and that to punish them all indiscriminately now suggested the court's mercy had not yet gone far enough.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，多所甄復。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and restored many of them to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and restored many of them to office.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Jingzong was moved to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Jingzong was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗饕沓，遂以女嫁蠻酋馮盎子，多私所聘。

translations.literal: Jingzong was greedy and grasping. He then married his daughter to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang, keeping much of the betrothal gifts for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and grasping, Jingzong married his daughter to the son of the southern chieftain Feng Ang and kept much of the betrothal wealth for himself.

sentences.zh: 有司劾舉，下除鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached him. He was demoted to Prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the responsible offices impeached him, he was demoted to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄復官，為弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to office as a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office as a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝將立武昭儀，大臣切諫，而敬宗陰揣帝私，即妄言曰：「田舍子剩獲十斛麥，尚欲更故婦。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to install Consort Wu Zhaoyi as empress. The great ministers remonstrated urgently. Jingzong secretly divined the emperor's private wish and rashly said: "A farmhand who has just harvested ten hu of wheat still wants to replace his old wife.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor meant to elevate Consort Wu to empress and the chief ministers protested sharply, Jingzong guessed his private wish and said rashly, "A farmer who has just harvested ten hu of wheat still wants to trade in his old wife.

sentences.zh: 天子富有四海，立一後，謂之不可，何哉？」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven possesses all within the four seas. To install one empress and say it cannot be done—how is this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven owns the realm—how can installing one empress be called impossible?"

sentences.zh: 帝意遂定。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: With that the emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 王後廢，敬宗請削後家官爵，廢太子忠而立代王，遂兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: When Empress Wang was deposed, Jingzong requested that the empress's family's titles and offices be stripped. He deposed Crown Prince Zhong and installed the Prince of Dai, and then concurrently served as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wang was deposed, Jingzong urged stripping her family's ranks and titles, deposing Crown Prince Zhong and installing the Prince of Dai; he then also served as mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝得所欲，故詔敬宗待詔武德殿西闥。

translations.literal: The emperor obtained what he desired. Therefore he ordered Jingzong to await imperial orders at the western side chamber of Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Having gotten his way, the emperor ordered Jingzong to await commands at the western side chamber of Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 頃拜侍中，監修國史，爵郡公。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Palace Attendant, supervised the compilation of national history, and was ennobled as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made palace attendant, put in charge of compiling the national history, and ennobled as duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸故長安城，按蹕裴回，視古區處，問侍臣：「秦、漢以來幾君都此？」

translations.literal: The emperor once visited the old city of Chang'an. Halting his escort he wandered about, viewing the ancient sites, and asked the attending ministers: "Since Qin and Han, how many rulers have made this their capital?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, touring the old city of Chang'an, the emperor paused his escort to wander the ancient sites and asked his attendants, "Since Qin and Han, how many rulers have made this their capital?"

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「秦居咸陽，漢惠帝始城之。

translations.literal: Jingzong said: "The Qin dwelt at Xianyang. Emperor Hui of Han first walled this place.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied, "The Qin ruled from Xianyang; Emperor Hui of Han was the first to wall this city.

sentences.zh: 其後苻堅、姚萇、宇文周居之。」

translations.literal: Afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Zhou of the Yuwen clan dwelt here."
translations.idiomatic: Later Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Yuwen Zhou also ruled from here."

sentences.zh: 帝復問：「漢武開昆明池實何年？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked again: "In what year did Emperor Wu of Han actually open Kunming Pool?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "In what year did Emperor Wu of Han actually open Kunming Pool?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「元狩三年，將伐昆明，實為此池以肄戰。」

translations.literal: He answered: "In the third year of Yuan-shuo, when he was about to attack Kunming, he in fact made this pool to drill for war."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In the third year of Yuan-shuo, when he was preparing to attack Kunming, he built this pool to train his fleet for war."

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔與弘文學士討古宮室故區，具條以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered him, together with the Hongwen scholars, to investigate ancient palaces and former sites and report item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered him and the Hongwen scholars to research ancient palaces and former sites and report their findings in full.

sentences.zh: 進中書令，仍守侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and still retained the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat while continuing to serve as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 敬宗於立後有助力，知後鉗戾，能固主以久己權，乃陰連後謀逐韓瑗、來濟、褚遂良，殺梁王、長孫無忌、上官儀，朝廷重足事之，威寵熾灼，當時莫與比。

translations.literal: Jingzong had helped in establishing the empress. Knowing that the empress was fierce and unyielding, he could secure her support to prolong his own power. He then secretly joined the empress in plotting to drive out Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Chu Suiliang, and to kill the Prince of Liang, Zhangsun Wuji, and Shangguan Yi. The court walked on tiptoe before him. His authority and favor blazed; none in his day could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Having helped install the empress, Jingzong knew how fierce and unyielding she was and secured her favor to prolong his own power. He secretly joined her in driving out Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Chu Suiliang and in destroying the Prince of Liang, Zhangsun Wuji, and Shangguan Yi. The court walked on tiptoe before him; his power and favor burned so hot that none in his day could rival him.

sentences.zh: 改右相，辭疾，拜太子少師、同東西臺三品。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Chancellor. Citing illness, he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Offices alike.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right chancellor, then pleaded illness and was appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent with third rank at both the eastern and western offices.

sentences.zh: 年老，不任趨步，特詔與司空李勣朝朔日，聽乘小馬至內省。

translations.literal: He was old and could not manage hurried steps. A special edict allowed him, together with Minister of Works Li Ji, to attend court on the first of the month and permitted him to ride a small horse to the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he could no longer keep pace on foot, so a special edict allowed him, like Minister of Works Li Ji, to attend only on the first of the month and to ride a pony as far as the inner offices.

sentences.zh: 帝東封泰山，以敬宗領使。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the eastern feng at Mount Tai, he made Jingzong lead the mission.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went east to perform the feng rite on Mount Tai, he put Jingzong in charge of the mission.

sentences.zh: 次濮陽，帝問竇德玄：「此謂帝丘，何也？」

translations.literal: Stopping at Puyang, the emperor asked Dou Dexuan: "This is called Diqiu—what does that mean?"
translations.idiomatic: At Puyang the emperor asked Dou Dexuan, "This place is called Diqiu—what does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 德玄不對。

translations.literal: Dexuan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan had no answer.

sentences.zh: 敬宗儳曰：「臣能知之。

translations.literal: Jingzong interjected: "Your servant knows.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong broke in, "Your servant knows.

sentences.zh: 昔帝顓頊始居此地，以王天下。

translations.literal: In antiquity Emperor Zhuanxu first dwelt in this place and ruled all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Emperor Zhuanxu first made this place his seat and ruled the realm.

sentences.zh: 其後夏後相因之，為寒浞所滅。

translations.literal: Afterward the Xia ruler Xiang followed him here and was destroyed by Han Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xia ruler Xiang held it too until he was destroyed by Han Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 後緡方侲，逃出自竇，在此地也。

translations.literal: Later Fang Zhen of Youqian escaped from the Dou clan and was in this place.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fang Zhen of Youqian fled the Dou clan and found refuge here.

sentences.zh: 後昆吾氏因之，而為夏伯。

translations.literal: Afterward the Kunwu clan followed and became Earl of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Kunwu clan held it and became earl of Xia.

sentences.zh: 昆吾既衰，湯滅之。

translations.literal: When Kunwu declined, Tang destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kunwu declined, Tang destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 其頌曰：『韋、顧既伐，昆吾、夏桀』是也。

translations.literal: The hymn says, "Wei and Gu having been attacked, Kunwu and Xia Jie"—this refers to that.
translations.idiomatic: As the hymn says, "Wei and Gu having been attacked, Kunwu and Xia Jie"—that is the event meant.

sentences.zh: 至春秋時，衛成公自楚丘徙居之，《左氏》稱『相奪予享』，以舊地也。

translations.literal: By the Spring and Autumn period Duke Cheng of Wei moved here from Chuqiu. The Zuo Commentary speaks of "Xiang seizing his sacrifice" because it was an old domain.
translations.idiomatic: By Spring and Autumn times Duke Cheng of Wei moved here from Chuqiu; the Zuo Commentary's line about "Xiang seizing his sacrifice" refers to this as an ancient seat.

sentences.zh: 由顓頊所居，故曰帝丘。

translations.literal: Because Zhuanxu dwelt here, it is therefore called Diqiu, the Hill of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhuanxu once dwelt here, the place is called Diqiu, the Hill of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 臣聞有德者啟其國土，失道者則喪其疆宇。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the virtuous open their states and lands, while those who lose the Way forfeit their territories.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the virtuous open their states and lands, while those who lose the Way forfeit their domains.

sentences.zh: 自古大都美國，居者不一姓，故有國家者不可不慎也。」

translations.literal: From antiquity great capitals and fair states have not been held by a single clan. Therefore those who possess a state cannot be inattentive."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity great capitals and fertile lands have never stayed with one clan, so rulers who hold a state cannot afford to be careless."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「《書》稱『浮於濟、漯』，今濟與漯斷不相屬，何故而然？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Documents say 'floating on the Ji and the Luo.' Today the Ji and the Luo are wholly unconnected. For what reason is this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Documents speak of 'floating on the Ji and the Luo,' yet today the Ji and the Luo no longer connect—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夏禹道沇水東流為濟，入於河。

translations.literal: He answered: "Yu of Xia directed the Yan River east to become the Ji and enter the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Yu of Xia directed the Yan River eastward to form the Ji, which entered the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 今自漯至溫而入河，水自此洑地過河而南，出為滎；

translations.literal: Now from the Luo to Wen it enters the river. The water from here surges underground, crosses the river to the south, and emerges as the Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Luo reaches the river at Wen; from there the water surges underground, crosses the Yellow River to the south, and emerges as the Ying.

sentences.zh: 又洑而至曹、濮，散出於地，合而東，汶水自南入之，所謂『泆為滎，東出於陶丘北，又東會於汶』是也。

translations.literal: It surges again to Cao and Pu, disperses above ground, reunites and flows east, and the Wen River enters from the south. This is what is meant by "the overflow becomes the Ying, flows east from north of Taoqiu, and again east joins the Wen."
translations.idiomatic: It surges again toward Cao and Pu, breaks out above ground, reunites and flows east, and the Wen enters from the south—this is the passage that says, "the overflow becomes the Ying, flows east from north of Taoqiu, and again east joins the Wen."

sentences.zh: 古者五行皆有官，水官不失職，則能辨味與色。

translations.literal: In antiquity each of the Five Phases had its officer. When the water officer did not neglect his duty, he could distinguish taste and color.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity each of the five phases had its officer; when the water officer did his duty he could tell taste and color apart.

sentences.zh: 潛而出，合而更分，皆能識之。」

translations.literal: Whether hidden underground or emerging, joining and again dividing—all could be recognized."
translations.idiomatic: Whether a stream ran hidden or surfaced, joined or split again, he could identify it."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下洪流巨谷，不載祀典，濟甚細而在四瀆，何哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Throughout the realm great floods and vast valleys are not recorded in the sacrificial canon. The Ji is very slight yet ranks among the Four Streams—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Great floods and vast valleys across the realm are not listed in the sacrificial canon—why is the Ji, so slight a stream, counted among the four sacred rivers?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「瀆之言獨也。

translations.literal: He answered: "Du means alone.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Du means alone.

sentences.zh: 不因餘水，獨能赴海者也。

translations.literal: It does not rely on other waters but alone can reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: It does not rely on other waters but reaches the sea on its own.

sentences.zh: 且天有五星，運而為四時；

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven has five stars, which in motion become the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has five stars, which in motion become the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 地有五嶽，流而為四瀆；

translations.literal: Earth has five sacred peaks, which in flowing become the four streams.
translations.idiomatic: earth has five sacred peaks, which in flowing become the four streams;

sentences.zh: 人有五事，用而為四支。

translations.literal: Man has five affairs, which in use become the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: and man has five faculties, which in use become the four limbs.

sentences.zh: 五，陽數也；

translations.literal: Five is the yang number.
translations.idiomatic: Five is the yang number;

sentences.zh: 四，陰數也，有奇偶、陰陽焉。

translations.literal: Four is the yin number. There are odd and even, yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: four is the yin number—there are odd and even, yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 陽者光曜，陰者晦昧，故辰隱而難見。

translations.literal: Yang is luminous; yin is obscure. Therefore the fifth star is hidden and hard to see.
translations.idiomatic: Yang shines forth, yin stays dim, so the fifth star is hidden and hard to see.

sentences.zh: 濟潛流屢絕，狀雖微細，獨而尊也。」

translations.literal: The Ji flows hidden and often breaks off. Though slight in appearance, it is alone and therefore honored."
translations.idiomatic: The Ji runs hidden and often breaks off; though slight in appearance, it is honored because it stands alone."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 敬宗退，矜曰：「大臣不可無學，向德玄不能對，吾恥之。」

translations.literal: When Jingzong withdrew he said proudly: "Great ministers cannot be without learning. Just now Dexuan could not answer—I am ashamed for him."
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzong withdrew he said with pride, "A great minister must be learned; I am ashamed that Dexuan could not answer just now."

sentences.zh: 德玄聞之，不屑曰：「人各有能。

translations.literal: When Dexuan heard this he said disdainfully: "Each man has his abilities.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexuan heard this he said disdainfully, "Each man has his own strengths.

sentences.zh: 不強所不知，吾所能也。」

translations.literal: Not to force what one does not know—that is what I can do."
translations.idiomatic: Not to force what one does not know—that is what I can do."

sentences.zh: 李勣曰：「敬宗多聞，美矣；

translations.literal: Li Ji said: "Jingzong is widely learned—fine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji said, "Jingzong is widely learned—that is admirable;

sentences.zh: 竇之不強，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: That Dou does not force himself—is that not also good?"
translations.idiomatic: is it not also good that Dou does not force himself?"

sentences.zh: 初，《高祖、太宗實錄》，敬播所撰，信而詳。

translations.literal: At first the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong were composed by Xu Jingbo and were trustworthy and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong, written by Xu Jingbo, were trustworthy and detailed.

sentences.zh: 及敬宗身為國史，竄改不平，專出己私。

translations.literal: When Jingzong himself became national historian, he altered what was not fair and issued only his private views.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzong himself held the national history, he altered the record unfairly and shaped it to serve his private ends.

sentences.zh: 始虞世基與善心同遭賊害，封德彜常曰：「昔吾見世基死，世南匍匐請代；

translations.literal: At first Yu Shiji and Shansin alike suffered harm from the rebels. Feng Deyi often said: "In the past I saw Shiji die. Shinan crawled on the ground and begged to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Shiji and Shansin alike fell victim to the rebels, Feng Deyi often said, "I once saw Shiji die while Shinan crawled on the ground begging to take his place;

sentences.zh: 善心死，敬宗蹈舞求生。」

translations.literal: When Shansin died, Jingzong danced and leapt to save his life."
translations.idiomatic: when Shansin died, Jingzong danced and capered to save his own life."

sentences.zh: 世為口實，敬宗銜憤。

translations.literal: This became a byword in the world. Jingzong harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The story became a byword, and Jingzong nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 至立《德彜傳》，盛誣以惡。

translations.literal: When he wrote the biography of Deyi, he heaped slanderous evil upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote Deyi's biography he heaped slander upon him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗子娶尉遲敬德女孫，而女嫁錢九隴子。

translations.literal: Jingzong's son married the granddaughter of Yuchi Jingde, while his daughter married the son of Qian Jiulong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's son married a granddaughter of Yuchi Jingde, and his daughter married a son of Qian Jiulong.

sentences.zh: 九隴，本高祖隸奴也，為虛立門閥功狀，至與劉文靜等同傳。

translations.literal: Jiulong had originally been a bondservant of Gaozu. Jingzong falsely set up his clan pedigree and record of merit, going so far as to place him in the same biography as Liu Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiulong had been one of Gaozu's bondsmen; Jingzong fabricated his pedigree and merits and even placed him in the same biography as Liu Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 太宗賜長孫無忌《威鳳賦》，敬宗猥稱賜敬德。

translations.literal: Taizong bestowed on Zhangsun Wuji the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix." Jingzong improperly said it was bestowed on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had given Zhangsun Wuji the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix," but Jingzong falsely recorded that it was given to Jingde.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋龐孝泰率兵從討高麗，賊笑其懦，襲破之。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Pang Xiaotai led troops in the campaign against Goguryeo. The enemy mocked his cowardice and attacked and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: The southern chieftain Pang Xiaotai led troops against Goguryeo; the enemy mocked his cowardice, attacked, and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗受其金，乃稱「屢破賊，唐將言驍勇者唯蘇定方與孝泰，曹繼叔、劉伯英出其下遠甚」。

translations.literal: Jingzong received his gold and then declared: "He repeatedly defeated the enemy. Among Tang generals famed for valor, only Su Dingfang and Xiaotai are spoken of; Cao Jishu and Liu Boying fall far below them."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong took his gold and then wrote that he had "repeatedly broken the enemy," and that among Tang generals famed for valor only Su Dingfang and Xiaotai were worth naming, with Cao Jishu and Liu Boying far beneath them.

sentences.zh: 然知貞觀後，論次諸書，自晉盡隋，及《東殿新書》、《西域圖志》、《姓氏錄》、《新禮》等數十種皆敬宗總知之，賞賚不勝紀。

translations.literal: Yet it is known that after Zhenguan, in arranging and compiling the various books—from Jin through Sui, as well as the Eastern Hall New Book, the Western Regions Gazetteer, the Register of Surnames, the New Rites, and several tens of other works—Jingzong had general oversight. Rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Zhenguan he oversaw the compilation of dozens of works, from histories spanning Jin through Sui to the Eastern Hall New Book, the Western Regions Gazetteer, the Register of Surnames, and the New Rites, and the rewards he received were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 敬宗營第舍華僭，至造連樓，使諸妓走馬其上，縱酒奏樂自娛。

translations.literal: Jingzong built a residence lavish beyond his rank, even constructing linked towers on which he had his courtesans ride horses, indulging in wine and music for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong built a mansion so lavish it exceeded his rank, even erecting linked towers where he had his courtesans race horses while he drank and made music for his own amusement.

sentences.zh: 嬖其婢，因以繼室，假姓虞。

translations.literal: He favored a maidservant and made her his successor wife, giving her the false surname Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He favored a maidservant, made her his successor wife, and gave her the false surname Yu.

sentences.zh: 子昂烝之，敬宗怒黜虞，奏斥昂嶺外，久乃表還。

translations.literal: His son Ang took her as a mistress. Jingzong in anger dismissed Yu, memorialized to exile Ang beyond the mountains, and only after a long time petitioned for his return.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Ang took her as a mistress, Jingzong in anger dismissed Yu, memorialized to exile Ang beyond the mountains, and only after a long interval petitioned for his return.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，以特進致仕，仍朝朔望，續其俸祿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianheng era he retired with the special advancement rank, yet still attended court on the first and fifteenth of the month, and his salary continued.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianheng era he retired with special advancement rank but still attended court on the first and fifteenth of each month, and his salary continued.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝為舉哀，詔百官哭其第，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him. He ordered the hundred officials to weep at his residence. By patent he was posthumously given Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Acting Three Excellencies and Great Governor-General of Yangzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, ordered the officials to weep at his residence, and posthumously enfeoffed him as grand master of the palace with golden seal and acting three excellencies and great governor-general of Yangzhou, with burial honors at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 太常博士袁思古議：「敬宗棄子荒僥，女嫁蠻落，謚曰繆。」

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong abandoned his son and was dissolute and extravagant. His daughter married into barbarian lands. His posthumous name should be Miu (False)."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Sigu, erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, proposed, "Jingzong abandoned his son, lived dissolutely, and married his daughter into the frontier—his posthumous name should be Miu, 'False.'

sentences.zh: 其孫彥伯訴思古有嫌，詔更議。

translations.literal: His grandson Yanbo complained that Sigu bore a grudge. An edict ordered reconsideration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yanbo protested that Sigu bore a grudge, and the emperor ordered the matter reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 博士王福畤曰：「何曾忠而孝，以食日萬錢謚繆醜，況敬宗忠孝兩棄，飲食男女之累過之。」

translations.literal: Erudite Wang Fuchou said: "He Zeng was loyal and filial, yet for eating ten thousand cash a day his posthumous name Miu was deemed ugly. How much more Jingzong, who abandoned both loyalty and filial piety and whose excesses in food, drink, and women surpassed him."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Fuchou said, "He Zeng was loyal and filial, yet because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food his posthumous name Miu was thought ugly—how much more Jingzong, who abandoned loyalty and filial piety alike and whose indulgence in food, drink, and women surpassed him."

sentences.zh: 執不改。

translations.literal: He held to his view and would not change it.
translations.idiomatic: He held to his view and would not change it.

sentences.zh: 有詔尚書省雜議，更謚曰恭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to discuss jointly, and the posthumous name was changed to Gong (Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Secretariat to discuss the matter jointly, and the posthumous name was changed to Gong, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 彥伯，昂子也，頗有文。

translations.literal: Yanbo was Ang's son and was quite accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, Ang's son, was quite accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 敬宗晚年不復下筆，凡大典冊悉彥伯為之。

translations.literal: In his later years Jingzong no longer put brush to paper. All great canonical works were done by Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Jingzong no longer wrote himself; Yanbo drafted all the great state documents.

sentences.zh: 嘗戲昂曰：「吾兒不及若兒。」

translations.literal: He once joked to Ang: "My son is not the equal of your son."
translations.idiomatic: He once teased Ang, "My son is not the equal of your son.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「渠父不如昂父。」

translations.literal: He replied, "His father is not the equal of Ang's father."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "His father is no match for Ang's father."

sentences.zh: 後又納婢譖，奏流彥伯嶺表，遇赦還，累官太子舍人。

translations.literal: Later he again took in a maid's slander, memorialized to exile Yanbo beyond the frontier passes; on encountering an amnesty he returned, and through successive appointments became Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again accepted a maid's slander and memorialized to have Yanbo exiled beyond the frontier. Yanbo returned on an amnesty and eventually rose to attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既與思古有憾，欲邀擊諸路，思古曰：「吾為先子報仇耳。」

translations.literal: Having a grievance with Sigu, he wanted to intercept and assault him on the road. Sigu said, "I merely avenged my late father."
translations.idiomatic: Because he bore a grudge against Sigu, he wanted to waylay and beat him on the road. Sigu said, "I was only avenging my late father.

sentences.zh: 彥伯慚而止。

translations.literal: Yanbo, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Yanbo desisted.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，詔敬宗配饗高宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, an edict ordered Jingzong to share sacrificial offerings in Emperor Gaozong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era, an edict ordered that Jingzong be given a place in Emperor Gaozong's temple to share in the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 李義府，瀛州饒陽人。

translations.literal: Li Yifu was a native of Raoyang in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu was a native of Raoyang in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其祖嘗為射洪丞，因客永泰。

translations.literal: His grandfather once served as assistant magistrate of Shehong and sojourned at Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had once served as assistant magistrate of Shehong and settled as a guest at Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，李大亮巡察劍南，表義府才，對策中第，補門下省典儀。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Li Daliang inspected Jiannan, memorialized Yifu's talent; he placed first in the policy examination and was appointed Master of Ceremonies in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, Li Daliang inspected Jiannan and recommended Yifu for his talent. Yifu placed first in the policy examination and was appointed master of ceremonies in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉洎、馬周更薦之，太宗召見，轉監察御史，詔侍晉王。

translations.literal: Liu Ji and Ma Zhou further recommended him. Taizong summoned him for audience. He was transferred to Supervising Censor and ordered to attend Prince Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and Ma Zhou recommended him further. Emperor Taizong summoned him for an audience, transferred him to supervising censor, and ordered him to attend Prince Jin.

sentences.zh: 王為太子，除舍人、崇賢館直學士，與司議郎來濟俱以文翰顯，時稱「來李」。

translations.literal: When the prince became heir apparent, Yifu was appointed Attendant and direct scholar of the Chongxian Hall. He and Policy Advisor Lai Ji were both distinguished for literary writing, and at the time they were called "Lai and Li."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, Yifu was made an attendant and direct scholar of the Chongxian Hall. He and policy advisor Lai Ji were both noted for their writing, and people at the time called them "Lai and Li."

sentences.zh: 獻《承華箴》，末云：「佞諛有類，邪巧多方。

translations.literal: He presented "Admonitions on Upholding Splendor," which ends: "Flattery has its kinds; craftiness takes many forms.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted "Admonitions on Upholding Splendor," which concludes, "Flattery comes in many kinds, and treacherous cunning takes many forms.

sentences.zh: 其萌不絕，其害必彰。」

translations.literal: If its sprouts are not cut off, its harm will surely be exposed."
translations.idiomatic: If its sprouts are not uprooted, the harm it does will surely become plain.

sentences.zh: 義府方諂事太子，而文致若讜直者，太子表之，優詔賜帛。

translations.literal: Yifu was at the time currying favor with the heir apparent, yet his writing feigned frank remonstrance. The heir memorialized about it, and an excellent edict awarded silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu was at that very time fawning on the heir apparent, yet his text was crafted to sound like blunt remonstrance. The heir memorialized about it, and the emperor responded with a gracious edict awarding silk.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，遷中書舍人，兼修國史，進弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer, concurrently edited the national history, and advanced to Hongwen Hall scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, Yifu was promoted to secretariat drafting officer, given concurrent charge of the national history, and advanced to Hongwen Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 為長孫無忌所惡，奏斥壁州司馬。

translations.literal: He was disliked by Zhangsun Wuji, who memorialized to demote him to military adjutant of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji disliked him and memorialized to have him demoted to military adjutant of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔未下，義府問計於舍人王德儉。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, Yifu sought advice from Attendant Wang Dejian.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict was issued, Yifu asked attendant Wang Dejian for advice.

sentences.zh: 德儉者，許敬宗甥，癭而智，善揣事，因曰：「武昭儀方有寵，上欲立為後，畏宰相議，未有以發之。

translations.literal: Dejian was Xu Jingzong's nephew — goitered but clever, skilled at gauging affairs. He said, "Consort Wu Zhao is just now favored. The emperor wishes to install her as empress but fears the chief ministers' discussion and has no way to broach it.
translations.idiomatic: Dejian was Xu Jingzong's nephew — goitered but clever and skilled at reading affairs. He said, "Consort Wu Zhao is just now in favor. The emperor wants to make her empress but fears what the chief ministers will say and has no way to bring the matter forward.

sentences.zh: 君能建白，轉禍於福也。」

translations.literal: If you can propose it, you may turn disaster into fortune."
translations.idiomatic: If you can propose it, you may turn misfortune into fortune.

sentences.zh: 義府即代德儉直夜，叩閣上表，請廢後立昭儀。

translations.literal: Yifu immediately replaced Dejian on night duty at the palace gate, knocked on the gate, and submitted a memorial requesting the deposal of the empress and installation of the Zhao Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu immediately took Dejian's place on night duty at the palace gate, knocked on the gate, and submitted a memorial asking that the empress be deposed and the Zhao Consort installed in her place.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，召見與語，賜珠一斗，停司馬詔書，留復侍。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, summoned him for conversation, bestowed a peck of pearls, halted the Bizhou adjutant edict, and kept him to attend again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, summoned him for an audience, bestowed a peck of pearls, halted the edict appointing him adjutant of Bizhou, and kept him at court to attend again.

sentences.zh: 武后已立，義府與敬宗、德儉及御史大夫崔義玄、中丞袁公瑜、大理正侯善業相推轂，濟其奸，誅棄骨鯁大臣，故後得肆誌攘取威柄，天子斂衽矣。

translations.literal: After Empress Wu was installed, Yifu with Jingzong, Dejian, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yixuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Gongyu, and senior justice Hou Shanye pushed one another forward, abetting his treachery and executing outspoken ministers. Thereafter he was able to indulge his designs and seize authority; the Son of Heaven drew in his robes before him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Empress Wu had been installed, Yifu together with Jingzong, Dejian, censor-in-chief Cui Yixuan, vice censor-in-chief Yuan Gongyu, and senior justice Hou Shanye egged one another on, abetting his treachery and executing outspoken ministers. Thereafter he was able to indulge his designs and seize power, and even the Son of Heaven drew in his robes before him.

sentences.zh: 義府貌柔恭，與人言，嬉怡微笑，而陰賊褊忌著於心，凡忤意者，皆中傷之，時號義府「笑中刀」。

translations.literal: Yifu looked gentle and respectful. When speaking with others he smiled pleasantly, yet treacherous narrow jealousy was fixed in his heart. Whoever crossed him he slandered. At the time they called Yifu "a blade within a smile."
translations.idiomatic: Yifu looked mild and deferential. When he spoke with others he smiled pleasantly, yet treachery and narrow jealousy were lodged in his heart. Anyone who crossed him he slandered. People at the time called Yifu "a blade hidden in a smile."

sentences.zh: 又以柔而害物，號曰「人貓」。

translations.literal: Also because he was soft yet harmed people, he was called "the human cat."
translations.idiomatic: Because he was soft-spoken yet harmed people, he was also called "the human cat."

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，封廣平縣男，又兼太子右庶子，爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery with Third Rank, enfeoffed as Baron of Guangping, also concurrently Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent; his nobility was raised to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery with third rank, enfeoffed as baron of Guangping, and also made right vice mentor of the heir apparent; his title was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 洛州女子淳於以奸系大理，義府聞其美，屬丞畢正義出之，納以為妾。

translations.literal: A woman of Luozhou, Chunyu, was imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review for adultery. Yifu heard she was beautiful and directed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi to release her; he took her as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Luozhou named Chunyu was imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard she was beautiful, told vice director Bi Zhengyi to release her, and took her as his concubine.

sentences.zh: 卿段竇玄以狀聞。

translations.literal: Minister Duan Jixuan reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Duan Jixuan reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 詔給事中劉仁軌、侍御史張倫鞫治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Attendant Liu Rengui and Attending Censor Zhang Lun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered attendant Liu Rengui and attending censor Zhang Lun to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 義府且窮，逼正義縊獄中以絕始謀。

translations.literal: Yifu was close to being cornered. He forced Zhengyi to hang himself in prison to cut off the initial plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu was nearly cornered. He forced Zhengyi to hang himself in prison so as to cut off the trail to the original scheme.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王義方廷劾，義府不引咎，三叱之，然後趨出。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Wang Yifang impeached him at court. Yifu did not acknowledge guilt; thrice he shouted at him, then hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Wang Yifang impeached him at court. Yifu refused to accept blame, shouted at him three times, and then hurried out.

sentences.zh: 義方極陳其惡，帝陰德義府，故貸不問，為抑義方，逐之。

translations.literal: Yifang fully laid out his crimes. The emperor secretly favored Yifu, so he pardoned and did not pursue the matter, and to suppress Yifang, drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yifang laid out his crimes in full. The emperor secretly favored Yifu, so he pardoned him and did not pursue the matter; to suppress Yifang, he had him driven away.

sentences.zh: 未幾進中書令，檢校御史大夫，加太子賓客，更封河間郡公，詔造私第。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, Acting Censor-in-Chief, added as Mentor of the Heir Apparent, further enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery; an edict ordered the building of a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to director of the Secretariat and acting censor-in-chief, made mentor of the heir apparent, and further enfeoffed as duke of Hejian commandery; an edict ordered a private residence built for him.

sentences.zh: 諸子雖褓負皆補清官。

translations.literal: Even his sons still in swaddling clothes were all given clean official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Even his sons still in swaddling clothes were all given respectable official posts.

sentences.zh: 初，杜正倫為黃門侍郎，義府才典儀。

translations.literal: At first Du Zhenglun was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Yifu was only Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At first Du Zhenglun was vice director of the Secretariat while Yifu was only master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及同輔政，正倫恃先進不相下，密與中書侍郎李友益圖去義府，反為所誣，交訟帝前。

translations.literal: When they jointly assisted government, Zhenglun relied on seniority and would not yield. Secretly with Vice Director Li Youyi he plotted to remove Yifu but was instead framed by him; they exchanged accusations before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When they served together as chief ministers, Zhenglun relied on seniority and would not defer to him. Secretly he and vice director Li Youyi plotted to remove Yifu, but Yifu framed them instead, and the two sides traded accusations before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝兩黜之，正倫為橫州刺史，義府普州刺史，流友益峰州。

translations.literal: The emperor demoted both: Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou, Yifu to prefect of Puzhou, and exiled Youyi to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted them both — Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou, Yifu to prefect of Puzhou — and exiled Youyi to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為吏部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as Minister of Personnel and Associate Director with Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as minister of personnel and associate director with third rank.

sentences.zh: 母喪免，奪喪為司列太常伯、同東西臺三品。

translations.literal: Dismission for mother's mourning; recalled from mourning as Minister of Ceremonial Arrangement and Associate of the Eastern and Western Chancellery with Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning, then was recalled from mourning as minister of ceremonial arrangement and associate of the eastern and western chancelleries with third rank.

sentences.zh: 更葬其先永康陵側，役縣人牛車輸土築墳，助役者凡七縣，高陵令不勝勞而死。

translations.literal: He reburied his ancestors beside Yongkang Tomb, conscripting county people and ox-carts to haul earth and build the mound. Helpers came from seven counties in all; the magistrate of Gaoling died from inability to bear the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He reburied his ancestors beside Yongkang Tomb, conscripting county people and ox-carts to haul earth and build the mound. Laborers were drawn from seven counties in all, and the magistrate of Gaoling died from the strain of the work.

sentences.zh: 公卿爭赗遺。

translations.literal: Grandees competed to send funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees competed to send funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 葬日，詔御史節哭。

translations.literal: On the burial day, an edict ordered censors to regulate weeping.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial, an edict ordered censors to regulate the mourning.

sentences.zh: 送車從騎相銜，帷帟奠帳自灞橋屬三原七十里不絕，需盾芻偶，僭侈不法，人臣送葬之盛無與比者。

translations.literal: Escort carriages and mounted attendants linked end to end; curtains and offering tents from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan for seventy li without break. Paraphernalia, shields, straw figures — extravagance beyond law. No minister's funeral equaled it.
translations.idiomatic: Escort carriages and mounted attendants stretched end to end; curtains and offering tents ran from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan for seventy li without interruption. Paraphernalia, shields, and straw figures made the display extravagantly unlawful. No minister's funeral had ever matched it.

sentences.zh: 殷王出閣，又兼府長史，稍遷右相。

translations.literal: When Prince Yin left the palace school, Yifu also served as chief administrator of his household; gradually he was promoted to right chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yin left the palace school, Yifu also served as chief administrator of his household, and gradually he was promoted to right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 義府已貴，乃言系出趙郡，與諸李敘昭穆，嗜進者往往尊為父兄行。

translations.literal: Once ennobled, Yifu claimed descent from Zhao commandery and arranged senior and junior relations with various Lis; the ambitious often honored him as an elder kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen high, Yifu claimed descent from Zhao commandery and arranged senior and junior kinship with various Lis; the ambitious often honored him as an elder kinsman.

sentences.zh: 給事中李崇德引與同譜，既謫普州，亟削去，義府銜之，及復當國，傅致其罪，使自殺於獄。

translations.literal: Attendant Li Chongde linked him to the same genealogy. Once demoted to Puzhou he swiftly cut the connection. Yifu resented it; when he again held power he fabricated crimes and made him commit suicide in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Li Chongde linked him to the same genealogy. Once Yifu was demoted to Puzhou, Chongde swiftly cut the connection. Yifu resented this, and when he again held power he fabricated crimes against him and had him commit suicide in prison.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，高士廉、韋挺、岑文本、令狐德棻修《氏族志》，凡升降，天下允其議，於是州藏副本以為長式。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, Gao Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen compiled the Record of Clans. All promotions and demotions — the realm approved their deliberations; thereafter each prefecture kept a copy as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, Gao Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen compiled the Record of Clans. The realm accepted their decisions on every promotion and demotion, and thereafter each prefecture kept a copy as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 時許敬宗以不載武后本望，義府亦恥先世不見敘，更奏刪正。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jingzong because Wu Hou's origins were not recorded, and Yifu also ashamed that his forebears were not mentioned, jointly memorialized to revise and correct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jingzong resented that Empress Wu's origins had not been recorded, and Yifu was ashamed that his own forebears had not been listed; together they memorialized to revise and correct the work.

sentences.zh: 委孔誌約、楊仁卿、史玄道、呂才等定其書，以仕唐官至五品皆升士流。

translations.literal: They entrusted Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lu Cai and others to fix the work: all who in Tang service reached fifth rank were elevated to gentry status.
translations.idiomatic: They entrusted Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lu Cai, and others to finalize the book, decreeing that anyone who in Tang service had reached fifth rank or above would be elevated to gentry status.

sentences.zh: 於是兵卒以軍功進者，悉入書限，更號《姓氏錄》，搢紳共嗤靳之，號曰「勛格」。

translations.literal: Thereupon soldiers promoted by military merit all entered the register's limits. Renamed Register of Surnames. Gentry jointly scoffed and stingily rejected it, calling it "Merit Register."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon soldiers promoted by military merit all entered the register. The work was retitled Register of Surnames. The gentry jointly scoffed at it and called it the "Merit Register."

sentences.zh: 義府奏悉收前誌燒絕之。

translations.literal: Yifu memorialized to collect all previous registers and burn them to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu memorialized to collect all the previous registers and burn them completely.

sentences.zh: 自魏太和中定望族，七姓子孫叠為婚姻，後雖益衰，猶相誇尚。

translations.literal: Since the Taihe era of Wei fixed the great clans, descendants of the seven surnames intermarried in succession. Later though increasingly in decline, they still mutually boasted and prized it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great clans had been fixed in the Taihe era of Wei, descendants of the seven surnames had intermarried generation after generation. Later, though they grew ever more diminished, they still prided themselves on it.

sentences.zh: 義府為子求婚不得，遂奏一切禁止。

translations.literal: Yifu sought marriage for his son but could not obtain it, so he memorialized to forbid it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu sought a marriage for his son but could not obtain one, so he memorialized to forbid such marriages altogether.

sentences.zh: 既主選，無品鑒才，而溪壑之欲，惟賄是利，不復銓判，人人咨訕。

translations.literal: Once in charge of selection, he had no talent for appraisal. Ravine-and-gully greed — only bribes profited him. He no longer evaluated and decided appointments; everyone murmured in reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was in charge of selection, he had no talent for judging men. His greed was bottomless and he cared only for bribes. He no longer evaluated and decided appointments, and everyone murmured against him.

sentences.zh: 又母、妻、諸子賣官市獄，門如沸湯。

translations.literal: Also his mother, wife, and sons sold offices and traded in prison cases; their gate was like boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, wife, and sons also sold offices and traded in prison cases, and their gate was as busy as boiling water.

sentences.zh: 自永徽後，御史多制授，吏部雖有調註，至門下覆不留。

translations.literal: Since Yonghui, many censors were appointees by decree. Though the Ministry of Personnel had assignments, at the Secretariat review none were retained.
translations.idiomatic: After Yonghui, many censors were appointed by direct decree. Even when the Ministry of Personnel made assignments, the Secretariat review rejected them all.

sentences.zh: 義府乃自註御史、員外、通事舍人，有司不敢卻。

translations.literal: Yifu himself registered censors, outside-section officials, and masters of ceremonial intercourse; the relevant offices dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu himself registered censors, outside-section officials, and masters of ceremonial intercourse, and the relevant offices dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容戒義府曰：「聞卿兒子女婿橈法多過失，朕為卿掩覆，可少勖之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once casually admonished Yifu: "I hear your sons and sons-in-law bend the law with many faults. I have covered for you — you should somewhat exhort them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once casually admonished Yifu, saying, "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law bend the law and commit many faults. I have covered for you — you should exhort them a little.

sentences.zh: 義府內倚後，揣群臣無敢白其罪者，不虞帝之知，乃勃然變色，徐曰：「誰為陛下道此？」

translations.literal: Yifu inwardly relied on the empress, reckoning none of the ministers would dare report his crimes, not expecting the emperor knew. He suddenly changed color and said slowly, "Who told Your Majesty this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yifu inwardly relied on the empress and assumed no minister would dare report his crimes, so he did not expect the emperor to know. He suddenly changed color and said slowly, "Who told Your Majesty this?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何用問我所從得邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What need to ask where I learned it from!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What need is there to ask where I learned it!"

sentences.zh: 義府謷然不謝，徐引去，帝由是不悅。

translations.literal: Yifu loudly did not thank him and slowly withdrew. From this the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu answered loudly without thanking him and withdrew slowly. From that point the emperor was displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 會術者杜元紀望義府第有獄氣，曰：「發積錢二千萬，可以厭勝。」

translations.literal: A diviner, Du Yuanji, viewing Yifu's residence, saw prison qi. He said, "Expend accumulated cash of twenty million and you can suppress and overcome it."
translations.idiomatic: A diviner named Du Yuanji, looking at Yifu's residence, saw an aura of imprisonment. He said, "Spend twenty million in accumulated cash and you can suppress and overcome it.

sentences.zh: 義府信之，裒索殊急。

translations.literal: Yifu believed it and searched and extorted with extraordinary urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu believed him and searched and extorted money with extraordinary urgency.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，朔望給告，即羸服與元紀出野，馮高窺覘災眚，眾疑其有異謀。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, on the first and fifteenth when leave was granted he wore mourning garb and went into the wilds with Yuanji, mounting high to peep at calamities and portents. The crowd suspected he had secret designs.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his mother, on the first and fifteenth of the month when leave was granted he would put on mourning garb and go into the countryside with Yuanji, climbing high to observe calamities and portents. People suspected he had secret designs.

sentences.zh: 又遣子津召長孫延，謂曰：「吾為子得一官。」

translations.literal: Also he sent his son Jin to summon Zhangsun Yan, saying, "I have obtained an office for you."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his son Jin to summon Zhangsun Yan and said, "I have obtained an office for you.

sentences.zh: 居五日，延拜司津監，索謝錢七十萬。

translations.literal: After five days Yan was appointed Supervisor of the Office of Ferries; they demanded thanks-money of seven hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Yan was appointed supervisor of the Office of Ferries, and they demanded seven hundred thousand in thank-you money.

sentences.zh: 右金吾倉曹參軍楊行穎白其贓，詔司刑太常伯劉祥道與三司雜訊，李勣監按，有狀，詔除名，流巂州，子率府長史洽、千牛備身洋及婿少府主簿柳元貞並流廷州，司議郎津流振州，朝野至相賀。

translations.literal: Right Golden Guard Warehouse Section Officer Yang Xingying reported his bribery. An edict ordered Minister of Punishment Liu Xiangdao with the Three Offices to conduct joint interrogation; Li Ji supervised the investigation. The charges were substantiated. An edict stripped his name from the rolls and exiled him to Qiongzhou. His sons Household Chief Administrator Zhi, Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant Yang, and son-in-law Palace Workshop Registrar Liu Yuanzhen were all exiled to Tingzhou; Policy Advisor Jin was exiled to Zhenzhou. Court and country congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingying, a warehouse section officer of the Right Golden Guard, reported his bribery. An edict ordered Liu Xiangdao, minister of punishment, to conduct a joint interrogation with the Three Offices under Li Ji's supervision. The charges were substantiated. Yifu was struck from the rolls and exiled to Qiongzhou. His sons Zhi and Yang, his son-in-law Liu Yuanzhen, and his son Jin were also exiled. Court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 三子及婿尤凶肆，既敗，人以為誅「四凶」。

translations.literal: The three sons and son-in-law were especially vicious and unrestrained. Once ruined, people considered it the execution of the "Four Evils."
translations.idiomatic: The three sons and the son-in-law had been especially vicious and unrestrained. Once they were ruined, people regarded it as the punishment of the "Four Evils."

sentences.zh: 或作《河間道元帥劉祥道破銅山大賊李義府露布》，榜於衢。

translations.literal: Someone wrote "Dispatch Proclamation of Hejian Circuit Commander-in-Chief Liu Xiangdao's Defeat of the Copper Mountain Great Bandit Li Yifu" and posted it in the thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote a dispatch proclamation titled "Hejian Circuit Commander Liu Xiangdao Defeats the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it in the streets.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年大赦，獨流人不許還，義府憤恚死，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng general amnesty, alone exiles were not permitted return. Yifu died of rage and resentment, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the general amnesty of the first year of Qianfeng, exiles alone were not permitted to return. Yifu died of rage and resentment at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 自其斥，天下憂且復用，比死，內外乃安。

translations.literal: From his dismissal the realm feared he might be reused. By his death, court and country were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of his dismissal the realm feared he might be employed again. Only when he died did court and country feel at ease.

sentences.zh: 上元初，赦妻子還洛陽。

translations.literal: Early in Shangyuan, his wife and children were pardoned and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan era, his wife and children were pardoned and allowed to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 如意中，贈義府揚州大都督，崔義玄益州大都督，王德儉、袁公瑜魏、相二州刺史，各賜實封。

translations.literal: In Ruyi, posthumously enfeoffed Yifu as Great Governor-General of Yangzhou, Cui Yixuan as Great Governor-General of Yizhou; Wang Dejian and Yuan Gongyu as prefects of Wei and Xiang prefectures; each granted substantive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ruyi era, Yifu was posthumously enfeoffed as great governor-general of Yangzhou, Cui Yixuan as great governor-general of Yizhou, and Wang Dejian and Yuan Gongyu as prefects of Wei and Xiang prefectures; each was granted a substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，詔停。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended, an edict halted this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, an edict halted these honors.

sentences.zh: 少子湛，見《李多祚傳》。

translations.literal: The youngest son Zhan — see Biography of Li Duozuo.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zhan is treated in the Biography of Li Duozuo.

sentences.zh: 傅遊藝，衛州汲人。

translations.literal: Fu Youyi was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youyi was a native of Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 載初初，由合宮主簿再遷左補闕。

translations.literal: At the very beginning of Zai Chu, from Clerk of the Palace of Universal Harmony he was twice promoted to Left Assistant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the very beginning of the Zai Chu era, he rose from clerk of the Palace of Universal Harmony through two promotions to left assistant censor.

sentences.zh: 武后奪政，即上書詭說符瑞，勸後當革姓以明受命。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu seized power, he immediately submitted a memorial with forced interpretations of portents, urging the empress to change the surname to manifest receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power, he immediately submitted a memorial with forced interpretations of portents, urging her to change the dynastic surname so as to manifest her receipt of the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 後悅，擢給事中。

translations.literal: The empress was pleased and promoted him to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was pleased and promoted him to attendant.

sentences.zh: 閱三月，進同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，即拜鸞臺侍郎。

translations.literal: Within three months he advanced to Associate Councilor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, and was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months he was advanced to associate councilor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace and immediately appointed vice director of the Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 後乃黜唐稱周，廢唐宗廟，自稱皇帝，賜遊藝姓武氏，以兄神童為冬官尚書。

translations.literal: Thereafter she abolished Tang for Zhou, dismantled the Tang ancestral temples, styled herself emperor, granted Youyi the surname Wu, and appointed his elder brother Shentong Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she abolished Tang in favor of Zhou, dismantled the Tang ancestral temples, styled herself emperor, granted Youyi the surname Wu, and appointed his elder brother Shentong minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 遊藝嘗夢登湛露殿，既寤，以語所親。

translations.literal: Youyi once dreamed of ascending the Hall of Pure Dew. On waking he told those close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi once dreamed that he had ascended the Hall of Pure Dew. When he woke he told those close to him.

sentences.zh: 有告其謀反者，下獄自殺，以五品禮葬之。

translations.literal: Someone reported him for plotting rebellion. He was imprisoned and committed suicide; he was buried with fifth-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that he was plotting rebellion. He was imprisoned and committed suicide, and was buried with fifth-rank rites.

sentences.zh: 初，遊藝探後旨，誣殺宗室，復請發六道使，後卒用其言。

translations.literal: At first Youyi sounded out the empress's intent, falsely killed imperial clansmen, and again requested dispatch of commissioners on six circuits; the empress ultimately adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: At first Youyi sounded out the empress's intent, falsely implicated and killed members of the imperial clan, and again requested the dispatch of commissioners on six circuits; the empress ultimately adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 萬國俊等既出，天下被其酷。

translations.literal: Once Wanguo Jun and others went out, the realm suffered their cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wanguo Jun and the others were dispatched, the realm suffered their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 遊藝起一歲，賜袍自青及紫，人號「四時仕宦」。

translations.literal: Youyi rose in one year; robes granted from azure to purple — people called him "Four-Seasons Officialdom."
translations.idiomatic: Youyi rose in a single year, receiving robes from azure to purple in succession, and people called him "an official for all four seasons."

sentences.zh: 然歲中即敗，前古少其比雲。

translations.literal: Yet within the year he fell — antiquity had few to compare with him, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the year he fell — antiquity had few like him, it is said.

sentences.zh: 李林甫，長平肅王叔良曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Linfu was great-grandson of Prince Su of Changping, Shuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was the great-grandson of Prince Su of Changping, Shuliang.

sentences.zh: 初為千牛直長，舅姜交愛之。

translations.literal: At first he was Chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard. His maternal uncle Jiang Jiao favored him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard, and his maternal uncle Jiang Jiao favored him.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he was transferred to Principal of the Heir Apparent's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was transferred to principal of the heir apparent's palace.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜執政，與交為姻家，而乾曜子為林甫求司門郎中，乾曜素薄之，曰：「郎官應得才望，哥奴豈郎中材邪？」

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao held power; he was related by marriage to Jiao. Qianyao's son sought the post of Director of the Office of Gates for Linfu. Qianyao always held him in low esteem and said, "Directors should have talent and repute — is Genun fit to be a director?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao was in power and was related by marriage to Jiang Jiao. Qianyao's son sought the post of director of the Office of Gates for Linfu, but Qianyao had always held him in low esteem and said, "Directors should have talent and standing — is Genun really fit to be a director?

sentences.zh: 哥奴，林甫小字也。

translations.literal: Genun was Linfu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Genun was Linfu's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 即授以諭德，累擢國子司業。

translations.literal: He was immediately given the post of Preceptor and through successive promotions rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was immediately given the post of preceptor and through successive promotions rose to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 宇文融為御史中丞，引與同列，稍歷刑、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Rong was Vice Censor-in-Chief, he brought Linfu onto the same roster; gradually he served as vice minister in Justice and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Rong was vice censor-in-chief, he brought Linfu onto the same roster, and Linfu gradually served as vice minister in the ministries of Justice and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部置長名榜，定留放。

translations.literal: At first the Ministry of Personnel set up the long-list roster to determine who stayed and who was released.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Ministry of Personnel maintained a long-list roster to determine who would be retained and who would be released.

sentences.zh: 寧王私謁十人，林甫曰：「願絀一人以示公。」

translations.literal: Prince Ning privately solicited for ten men. Linfu said, "I wish to demote one person to show you fairness."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning privately solicited on behalf of ten men. Linfu said, "I wish to demote one person to show you that I am fair.

sentences.zh: 遂榜其一，曰：「坐王所囑，放冬集。」

translations.literal: He then listed one, saying, "Because of the prince's request, released to the winter roster."
translations.idiomatic: He then listed one of them, noting, "At the prince's request, released to the winter roster."

sentences.zh: 時武惠妃寵傾後宮，子壽王、盛王尤愛。

translations.literal: At the time Consort Wu Huifei monopolized favor in the inner palace; her sons the Prince of Shou and Prince of Sheng were especially beloved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Consort Wu Huifei monopolized favor in the inner palace, and her sons the Prince of Shou and the Prince of Sheng were especially beloved.

sentences.zh: 林甫因中人白妃，願護壽王為萬歲計，妃德之。

translations.literal: Linfu through a eunuch told the consort he wished to protect the Prince of Shou for the long-term plan; the consort was grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu told the consort through a eunuch that he wished to protect the Prince of Shou for the long term, and the consort was grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 侍中裴光庭夫人，武三思女，嘗私林甫，而高力士本出三思家。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Guangting's wife, daughter of Wu Sansi, had once been intimate with Linfu; and Gao Lishi originally came from Sansi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Guangting's wife, a daughter of Wu Sansi, had once been intimate with Linfu, and Gao Lishi had originally come from Sansi's household.

sentences.zh: 及光庭卒，武請力士以林甫代為相。

translations.literal: When Guangting died, Wu asked Lishi to have Linfu replace him as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangting died, Wu asked Lishi to have Linfu replace him as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 力士未敢發，而帝因蕭嵩言，自用韓休。

translations.literal: Lishi did not dare to broach it, but the Emperor, on Xiao Song's words, on his own employed Han Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi did not dare to raise the matter, but the Emperor, acting on Xiao Song's recommendation, appointed Han Xiu on his own.

sentences.zh: 方具詔，武擿語林甫，使為休請。

translations.literal: Just as the edict was being prepared, Wu revealed it to Linfu and had him plead for Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the edict was being drafted, Wu tipped off Linfu and had him intercede on Han Xiu's behalf.

sentences.zh: 休既相，重德林甫，而與嵩有隙，乃薦林甫有宰相才，妃陰助之，即拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Once Xiu became chancellor, he deeply esteemed Linfu, but had a rift with Song; he therefore recommended that Linfu had chancellor talent, the consort secretly helped him, and he was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han Xiu became chancellor, he held Linfu in high regard, but he and Xiao Song were at odds; he therefore recommended Linfu as chancellor material. The consort secretly backed the move, and Linfu was promptly appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋為禮部尚書、同中書門下三品，再進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he became Minister of Rites and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Third Rank; he was again promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Rites and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Third Rank, and later promoted again to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、鄂王、光王被譖，帝欲廢之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, the Prince of E, and the Prince of Guang were slandered; the Emperor wished to depose them.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince, the Prince of E, and the Prince of Guang fell victim to slander, and the Emperor wished to depose them.

sentences.zh: 張九齡切諫，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling remonstrated sharply; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling remonstrated forcefully, and the Emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 林甫惘然，私語中人曰：「天子家事，外人何與邪？」

translations.literal: Linfu looked blank and privately said to a palace attendant: "This is the Son of Heaven's family affair—what business is it of outsiders?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu looked blank and quietly told a palace attendant, "This is the Son of Heaven's own family business—what business is it of outsiders?"

sentences.zh: 二十四年，帝在東都，欲還長安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Emperor was at the Eastern Capital and wished to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the Emperor was at the Eastern Capital and wished to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿等建言：「農人場圃未畢，須冬可還。」

translations.literal: Pei Yaoqing and others advised: "The farmers have not yet finished their threshing floors and gardens; one must wait until winter to return."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing and others advised, "The farmers have not yet finished work in their fields and orchards; the court should wait until winter before returning."

sentences.zh: 林甫陽蹇，獨在後。

translations.literal: Linfu feigned lameness and alone lingered behind.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu feigned lameness and hung back alone.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，對曰：「臣非疾也，願奏事。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your servant is not ill; I wish to report a matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked why; he replied, "I am not ill, Your Majesty; I wish to report a matter.

sentences.zh: 二都本帝王東西宮，車駕往幸，何所待時？

translations.literal: The two capitals are originally the Son of Heaven's eastern and western palaces—why must the imperial carriage wait for a season to visit?
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals are the Son of Heaven's eastern and western palaces—why must the imperial progress wait for the right season?

sentences.zh: 假令妨農，獨赦所過租賦可也。」

translations.literal: Even if it should hinder farming, it would suffice to remit rent and taxes along the route alone."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the journey should disrupt farming, it would be enough to remit rent and taxes along the route."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，即駕而西。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and immediately set out westward.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and immediately set out for the west.

sentences.zh: 始九齡繇文學進，守正持重，而林甫特以便佞，故得大任，每嫉九齡，陰害之。

translations.literal: At first Jiuling had risen through literary scholarship, holding integrity and weightiness, whereas Linfu relied solely on flattery and sycophancy to win great trust; he always envied Jiuling and secretly harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling had risen through scholarship and held fast to integrity and dignity, while Linfu won great trust through flattery alone; he always envied Jiuling and worked secretly to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲進朔方節度使牛仙客實封，九齡謂林甫：「封賞待名臣大功，邊將一上最，可遽議？

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to grant Shuo-fang Military Commissioner Niu Xianke enfeoffment with actual revenue; Jiuling told Linfu: "Enfeoffment and rewards await famous ministers with great merit—a frontier commander with one top performance rating, can one hastily consider it?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to grant Shuo-fang Military Commissioner Niu Xianke an enfeoffment with actual revenue. Jiuling told Linfu, "Rewards and enfeoffment are for famous ministers with great achievements—can we rush to grant them when a frontier general submits one top performance rating?

sentences.zh: 要與公固爭。」

translations.literal: I mean to argue this firmly with you."
translations.idiomatic: I intend to fight this out with you."

sentences.zh: 林甫然許。

translations.literal: Linfu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu agreed.

sentences.zh: 及進見，九齡極論，而林甫抑嘿，退又漏其言。

translations.literal: When they went in to audience, Jiuling argued to the utmost, while Linfu kept silent and restrained; after withdrawing he leaked Jiuling's words.
translations.idiomatic: When they went in to audience, Jiuling argued his case to the hilt, while Linfu held his tongue; after they withdrew, he leaked Jiuling's words.

sentences.zh: 仙客明日見帝，泣且辭。

translations.literal: The next day Xianke saw the Emperor, weeping and declining.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xianke appeared before the Emperor, weeping and declining the honor.

sentences.zh: 帝滋欲賞仙客，九齡持不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor all the more wished to reward Xianke; Jiuling steadfastly opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor only wanted more to reward Xianke, but Jiuling stood firm against it.

sentences.zh: 林甫為人言：「天子用人，何不可者？」

translations.literal: Linfu said to others: "When the Son of Heaven employs a man, what cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu told others, "When the Son of Heaven chooses a man for office, what is there that cannot be done?"

sentences.zh: 帝聞，善林甫不專也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he approved that Linfu was not obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard this, he approved Linfu for not being obstinate.

sentences.zh: 由是益疏薄九齡，俄與耀卿俱罷政事，專任林甫，相仙客矣。

translations.literal: From this the Emperor grew ever more distant and cold toward Jiuling; before long both he and Yaoqing were removed from state affairs, Linfu was entrusted alone, and Xianke was made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Emperor grew ever colder toward Jiuling; before long both he and Yaoqing were removed from office, Linfu was given sole charge of affairs, and Xianke was made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，三宰相就位，二人磬折趨，而林甫在中，軒驁無少讓，喜津津出眉宇間。

translations.literal: At first, when the three chancellors took their places, the other two bowed deeply and hurried forward, whereas Linfu stood in the middle, haughty and yielding not the slightest, delight brimming in his face.
translations.idiomatic: When the three chancellors first took their places, the other two bowed low and hurried forward, while Linfu stood in the middle, proud and unyielding, delight brimming from his brow.

sentences.zh: 觀者竊言：「一雕挾兩兔。」

translations.literal: Observers whispered: "One hawk holds two rabbits.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers whispered, "One hawk has caught two rabbits.

sentences.zh: 少選，詔書出，耀卿、九齡以左右丞相罷，林甫嘻笑曰：「尚左右丞相邪？」

translations.literal: Before long the edict appeared: Yaoqing and Jiuling were dismissed as Left and Right Chief Ministers. Linfu laughed and said: "Still Left and Right Chief Ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the edict appeared: Yaoqing and Jiuling were dismissed as Left and Right Chief Ministers. Linfu laughed and said, "Still Left and Right Chief Ministers?"

sentences.zh: 目恚而送乃止，公卿為戰栗。

translations.literal: He glared angrily as they were sent off before stopping; the nobles and ministers trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: He glared after them angrily as they were dismissed, then stopped; the nobles and ministers trembled.

sentences.zh: 於是林甫進兼中書令。

translations.literal: Thereupon Linfu was promoted and additionally made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Linfu was promoted and additionally appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝卒用其言，殺三子，天下冤之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately followed his words and killed the three princes; all under Heaven considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ultimately took his advice and executed the three princes; all under Heaven regarded it as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 大理卿徐嶠妄言：「大理獄殺氣盛，鳥雀不敢棲。

translations.literal: Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Jiao falsely claimed: "In the Court of Judicial Review the killing air runs strong, and birds dare not perch.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Jiao falsely claimed, "The Court of Judicial Review is so steeped in killing that birds dare not perch there.

sentences.zh: 今刑部斷死，歲才五十八，而烏鵲巢獄戶，幾至刑措。」

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Justice sentences only fifty-eight to death this year, and crows and magpies nest in the prison gates—it nearly reaches the point where punishments are set aside."
