translations.idiomatic: This year the Ministry of Justice has sentenced only fifty-eight men to death, and crows and magpies nest in the prison gates—we are nearly at the point where punishments need not be used at all."

sentences.zh: 群臣賀帝，而帝推功大臣，封林甫晉國公，仙客豳國公。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers congratulated the Emperor, and the Emperor attributed the merit to his great ministers, enfeoffing Linfu as Duke of Jin and Xianke as Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers congratulated the Emperor, who credited his great ministers and enfeoffed Linfu as Duke of Jin and Xianke as Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 及帝將立太子，林甫探帝意，數稱道壽王，語秘不傳，而帝意自屬忠王，壽王不得立。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to establish the Crown Prince, Linfu sounded out the Emperor's intent and repeatedly praised Prince Shou; his words were secret and unreported, but the Emperor's heart was set on Prince Zhong, so Prince Shou was not established.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was about to name a Crown Prince, Linfu probed his intent and repeatedly praised Prince Shou; his words were kept secret, but the Emperor's heart was set on Prince Zhong, and Prince Shou was not chosen.

sentences.zh: 太子既定，林甫恨謀不行，且畏禍，乃陽善韋堅。

translations.literal: Once the Crown Prince was established, Linfu resented that his scheme had failed and also feared reprisal; he therefore feigned goodwill toward Wei Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Crown Prince was established, Linfu resented the failure of his plot and feared reprisal; he therefore pretended to treat Wei Jian kindly.

sentences.zh: 堅，太子妃兄也。

translations.literal: Jian was the Crown Prince's consort's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian was the elder brother of the Crown Prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 使任要職，將覆其家，以搖東宮。

translations.literal: He had him appointed to important posts, intending to overturn his household to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He placed him in important posts, intending to bring down his household and undermine the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 乃構堅獄，而太子絕妃自明，林甫計黜。

translations.literal: He then constructed a case against Jian, but the Crown Prince repudiated his consort to clear himself, and Linfu's scheme was thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: He then fabricated a case against Jian, but the Crown Prince repudiated his consort to clear himself, and Linfu's scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 杜良娣之父有鄰與婿柳勣不相中，勣浮險，欲助林甫，乃上有鄰變事，捕送詔獄賜死。

translations.literal: Du Liangdi's father Youlin and his son-in-law Liu Ji were at odds; Ji was reckless and treacherous and wished to aid Linfu; he therefore submitted a report of Youlin's seditious conduct, had him arrested and sent to the imperial prison, and he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Du Liangdi's father Youlin and his son-in-law Liu Ji were at odds. Liu Ji was reckless and treacherous and wished to help Linfu; he submitted a report accusing Youlin of sedition, had him arrested and sent to the imperial prison, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 逮引裴敦復、李邕等，皆林甫素忌惡者，株連殺之。

translations.literal: The case was extended to implicate Pei Dunfu, Li Yong, and others—all men Linfu had long envied and hated—and they were killed in linked prosecutions.
translations.idiomatic: The case was extended to implicate Pei Dunfu, Li Yong, and others—all men Linfu had long hated—and they were executed in a chain of linked prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 太子亦出良娣為庶人。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also demoted Liangdi to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince also demoted Liangdi to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擿濟陽別駕魏林，使誣河西節度使王忠嗣欲擁兵佐太子。

translations.literal: Before long he prompted Jiyang Assistant Administrator Wei Lin to accuse Hexi Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi of wishing to raise troops to support the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he prompted Jiyang Assistant Administrator Wei Lin to accuse Hexi Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi of plotting to raise troops in support of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 帝不信，然忠嗣猶斥去。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not believe it, yet Zhongsi was nevertheless dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not believe the accusation, but Zhongsi was dismissed nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 林甫數曰：「太子宜知謀。」

translations.literal: Linfu repeatedly said: "The Crown Prince surely ought to know of the plot."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu kept saying, "The Crown Prince must surely have known of the plot."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾兒在內，安得與外人相聞？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "My son is within the palace—how could he be in contact with outsiders?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "My son lives within the palace—how could he be in contact with outsiders?

sentences.zh: 此妄耳！」

translations.literal: This is nonsense!"
translations.idiomatic: This is nonsense!"

sentences.zh: 林甫數危太子，未得志，一日從容曰：「古者立儲君必先賢德，非有大勛力於宗稷，則莫若元子。」

translations.literal: Linfu repeatedly endangered the Crown Prince yet did not achieve his aim; one day he said at leisure: "In antiquity, when establishing an heir one first looked for virtue and worth; unless one had great meritorious service to the altars of state, none was better than the eldest son."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu repeatedly moved against the Crown Prince without success; one day he said casually, "In antiquity an heir was chosen first for virtue and talent; unless a prince had rendered great service to the altars of state, none was better than the eldest son."

sentences.zh: 帝久之曰：「慶王往年獵，為豽傷面甚。」

translations.literal: After a long while the Emperor said: "In earlier years when Prince Qing went hunting, a badger wounded his face badly."
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the Emperor said, "Years ago, when Prince Qing went hunting, a badger badly scarred his face."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「破面不愈於破國乎？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Is a scarred face not better than a broken realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu replied, "Is a scarred face not better than a broken kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 帝頗惑，曰：「朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was quite unsettled and said: "I will consider this gradually.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was unsettled and said, "I will think on this in time.

sentences.zh: 然太子自以謹孝聞，內外無惎言，故飛語不得入，帝無所發其猜。

translations.literal: Yet the Crown Prince was known for diligence and filial piety, and there was no slander within or without; thus malicious gossip could not enter, and the Emperor had no opening to give vent to his suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Crown Prince was known for diligence and filial piety, and no slander arose within or without the court; malicious rumors could not take hold, and the Emperor had no opening to act on his suspicions.

sentences.zh: 林甫善刺上意，時帝春秋高，聽斷稍怠，厭繩檢，重接對大臣，及得林甫，任之不疑。

translations.literal: Linfu excelled at probing the sovereign's mind; by then the Emperor was advanced in years, his attention to judgments had slackened somewhat, he wearied of restraint, and he valued daily audience with his great ministers; once he had Linfu, he entrusted him without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu excelled at reading the sovereign's mind. By then the Emperor was advanced in years, his attention to governance had slackened, he had grown weary of restraint, and he valued easy daily contact with his ministers; once he had Linfu, he entrusted him without reservation.

sentences.zh: 林甫善養君欲，自是帝深居燕適，沈蠱衽席，主德衰矣。

translations.literal: Linfu was skilled at gratifying the sovereign's desires; from this the Emperor withdrew deep into pleasure and ease, sunk in indulgence upon his couch, and the sovereign's virtue declined.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was skilled at indulging the sovereign's desires; from then on the Emperor withdrew into pleasure, sunk in sensual ease upon his couch, and the sovereign's virtue waned.

sentences.zh: 林甫每奏請，必先餉遺左右，審伺微旨，以固恩信，至饔夫禦婢皆所款厚，故天子動靜必具得之。

translations.literal: Whenever Linfu submitted a memorial or request, he would first send gifts to those around the Emperor, carefully watch for subtle hints of intent to consolidate grace and trust—even cooks and palace maidservants he treated warmly—so that the Son of Heaven's every movement was fully known to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Linfu submitted a memorial or request, he first sent gifts to those around the Emperor and watched carefully for the slightest hint of his mood to secure favor—even cooks and palace maidservants he treated generously—so that he knew the Son of Heaven's every move.

sentences.zh: 性陰密，忍誅殺，不見喜怒。

translations.literal: His nature was secretive and dark; he could endure ordering executions and showed neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: Secretive by nature, he could order executions without flinching and showed neither joy nor anger.

sentences.zh: 面柔令，初若可親，既崖阱深阻，卒不可得也。

translations.literal: His face was soft and his words mild; at first he seemed approachable, but once pitfalls grew deep and barriers high, in the end one could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: His face was gentle and his words mild; at first he seemed approachable, but once his traps were set and his barriers raised, no one could reach him in the end.

sentences.zh: 公卿不由其門而進，必被罪徙；

translations.literal: If nobles and ministers advanced without going through his gate, they were inevitably convicted and banished;
translations.idiomatic: Any noble or minister who rose without going through his gate was inevitably convicted and banished;

sentences.zh: 附離者，雖小人且為引重。

translations.literal: those who attached themselves to him, even low men, would be given weight and recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: those who attached themselves to him, even base men, would be given weight and backing.

sentences.zh: 同時相若九齡、李適之皆遭逐；

translations.literal: Contemporary chancellors such as Jiuling and Li Shizhi were all driven out;
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary chancellors such as Jiuling and Li Shizhi were all driven out;

sentences.zh: 至楊慎矜、張瑄、盧幼臨、柳升等緣坐數百人，並相繼誅。

translations.literal: as far as Yang Shenjin, Zhang Xuan, Lu Youlin, Liu Sheng, and others—hundreds implicated by association—were executed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenjin, Zhang Xuan, Lu Youlin, Liu Sheng, and others—hundreds implicated by association—were executed one after another.

sentences.zh: 以王鉷、吉溫、羅希奭為爪牙，數興大獄，衣冠為累息。

translations.literal: With Wang Hong, Ji Wen, and Luo Xishi as his claws and fangs, he repeatedly raised great prosecutions, and the gentry and officials lived in unceasing dread.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Hong, Ji Wen, and Luo Xishi as his claws and fangs, he repeatedly launched great prosecutions, and the gentry and officials lived in constant dread.

sentences.zh: 適之子霅嘗盛具召賓客，畏林甫，乃終日無一人往者。

translations.literal: Shizhi's son Zha once prepared a lavish banquet and invited guests, but out of fear of Linfu not a single person came all day long.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's son Zha once laid out a lavish feast for guests, but out of fear of Linfu not a single person came all day.

sentences.zh: 林甫有堂如偃月，號月堂。

translations.literal: Linfu had a hall shaped like a crescent moon, called the Moon Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had a hall shaped like a crescent moon, called the Moon Hall.

sentences.zh: 每欲排構大臣，即居之，思所以中傷者。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to plot against a great minister, he would dwell there and ponder how to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wished to plot against a great minister, he would retire there and brood over how to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 若喜而出，即其家碎矣。

translations.literal: If he emerged pleased, that man's household would be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If he emerged smiling, that man's household was finished.

sentences.zh: 子岫為將作監，見權勢熏灼，惕然懼，常從遊後園，見輦重者，跪涕曰：「大人居位久，枳棘滿前，一旦禍至，欲比若人可得乎？」

translations.literal: His son Xiu was Director of Palace Construction; seeing how fiercely his power blazed, he grew fearful and alarmed. Often while following him in the rear garden, when he saw heavy imperial carriages, he would kneel in tears and say: "Father, you have held office long; thorns fill the path before you. Once disaster comes, can you hope to be like those men?"
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu was Director of Palace Construction. Seeing how fiercely his father's power burned, he grew fearful. Often while walking with him in the rear garden, when he saw heavy imperial carriages pass, he would kneel in tears and say, "Father, you have held office so long that thorns fill the path before you. When disaster strikes, can you hope to end like those men?"

sentences.zh: 林甫不樂曰：「勢已然，可奈何？」

translations.literal: Linfu, displeased, said: "The momentum is already set—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, displeased, said, "The momentum is already set—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 時帝詔天下士有一藝者得詣闕就選，林甫恐士對詔或斥己，即建言：「士皆草茅，未知禁忌，徒以狂言亂聖聽，請悉委尚書省長官試問。」

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor decreed that scholars throughout the realm who possessed a single skill might come to the palace gate for selection; Linfu feared that when scholars answered the decree they might denounce him, so he advised: "Scholars are all rustic commoners who know not taboos; they would merely use wild talk to confuse the holy ears. Please entrust all of them to the senior officials of the Secretariat for examination."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor decreed that any scholar in the realm with a single skill might come to the palace gate for selection. Linfu feared that some might use the audience to denounce him, so he advised, "These men are rustic commoners who know nothing of court taboos; they would only speak recklessly and confuse Your Majesty's judgment. Please have the senior officials of the Secretariat examine them all."

sentences.zh: 使御史中丞監總，而無一中程者。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief was made to supervise the whole, and not one passed the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Censor-in-Chief was put in charge of the examinations, and not one candidate passed.

sentences.zh: 林甫因賀上，以為野無留才。

translations.literal: Linfu thereupon congratulated the sovereign, holding that in the wilds no talent remained unselected.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu then congratulated the sovereign, declaring that no talent had been left untapped in the realm.

sentences.zh: 俄兼隴右、河西節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he additionally served as Military Commissioner of Longyou and Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he additionally served as Military Commissioner of Longyou and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 改右相，罷節度，加累開府儀同三司，實封戶三百。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Chancellor, relieved of the military commission, and additionally granted successive honors as Grand Master with Splendid Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, with an enfeoffment of three hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Chancellor, relieved of his military commission, and additionally granted successive honors as Grand Master with Splendid Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, with an enfeoffment of three hundred actual households.

sentences.zh: 咸寧太守趙奉璋得林甫隱惡二十條，將言之，林甫諷御史捕系奉璋，劾妖言，抵死；

translations.literal: Xianning Prefect Zhao Fengzhang obtained twenty articles of Linfu's hidden evils and was about to report them; Linfu hinted to the censors to arrest and imprison Fengzhang, charged him with heterodox speech, and he was punished with death;
translations.idiomatic: Xianning Prefect Zhao Fengzhang obtained twenty counts of Linfu's hidden crimes and was about to report them. Linfu prompted the censors to arrest Fengzhang, charged him with seditious speech, and he was put to death;

sentences.zh: 著作郎韋子春坐厚善貶。

translations.literal: Compilation Official Wei Zichun was demoted on account of close friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation Official Wei Zichun was demoted for being on close terms with Fengzhang.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗大陳樂勤政樓，既罷，兵部侍郎盧絢按轡絕道去，帝愛其藉，稱美之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once held great music at the Hall of Diligence in Governance; when it ended, Vice Minister of War Lu Xuan spurred his horse and left by a cleared road; the Emperor admired his mat and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once held a great musical performance at the Hall of Diligence in Governance. When it ended, Vice Minister of War Lu Xuan rode off along a cleared road, reins in hand; the Emperor admired his bearing and praised him.

sentences.zh: 明日林甫召絢子曰：「尊府素望，上欲任以交、廣，若憚行，且當請老。」

translations.literal: The next day Linfu summoned Xuan's son and said: "Your father's longstanding reputation is such that the sovereign wishes to appoint him to Jiao and Guang; if you shrink from the journey, he ought at least to request retirement."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Linfu summoned Xuan's son and said, "Your father enjoys great standing, and the sovereign wishes to appoint him to Jiao and Guang. If he dreads the posting, he should at least request retirement."

sentences.zh: 絢懼，從之。

translations.literal: Xuan was afraid and complied.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was frightened and complied.

sentences.zh: 因出為華州刺史，俄授太子員外詹事，絢繇是廢。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as Prefect of Hua, and soon appointed Supernumerary Household Steward of the Crown Prince; from this Xuan was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Prefect of Hua, and soon appointed Supernumerary Household Steward of the Crown Prince—a post that effectively ended his career.

sentences.zh: 於時有以材譽聞者，林甫護前，皆能得於天子抑遠之，故在位恩寵莫比。

translations.literal: At that time those who were known for talent and renown—Linfu, jealous and defensive, was able through the Son of Heaven to suppress and distance them all; thus in office his favor and grace had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone of talent and reputation emerged, Linfu—jealous and defensive—was able through the Son of Heaven to have them suppressed and sent away; thus no one in office enjoyed favor to match his.

sentences.zh: 凡禦府所貢遠方珍鮮，使者傳賜相望。

translations.literal: All rare delicacies from distant places that the imperial storehouse received were relayed to him by messengers in an unbroken stream of gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Rare delicacies from distant places sent to the imperial storehouse were relayed to him in an unbroken stream of gifts.

sentences.zh: 帝食有所甘美，必賜之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor's food brought some delicacy he enjoyed, he invariably granted it to Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor tasted something he enjoyed, he invariably sent a portion to Linfu.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔百僚閱歲貢於尚書省，既而舉貢物悉賜林甫，輦致其家。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor ordered the hundred officials to review the year's tribute at the Secretariat; afterward all the tribute items were granted to Linfu and carted to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor had the hundred officials review the year's tribute at the Secretariat; afterward every item of tribute was granted to Linfu and carted to his home.

sentences.zh: 從幸華清宮，給御馬、武士百人、女樂二部。

translations.literal: When he accompanied the Emperor to Huaqing Palace, he was supplied with imperial horses, a hundred warrior guards, and two companies of female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the Emperor to Huaqing Palace, he was given imperial horses, a hundred warrior guards, and two troupes of female musicians.

sentences.zh: 薛王別墅勝麗甲京師，以賜林甫，它邸第、田園、水硙皆便好上腴。

translations.literal: Prince Xue's villa, surpassing all in loveliness in the capital, was granted to Linfu; his other mansions, fields, gardens, and water-powered mills were all choice, convenient, and on rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xue's villa, the finest in the capital, was granted to Linfu; his other mansions, fields, gardens, and water mills were all choice properties on rich land.

sentences.zh: 車馬衣服侈靡，尤好聲伎。

translations.literal: His carriages, horses, and clothing were extravagantly luxurious; he especially loved music and performers.
translations.idiomatic: His carriages, horses, and clothing were extravagantly luxurious, and he was especially fond of music and performers.

sentences.zh: 侍姬盈房，男女五十人。

translations.literal: His concubines filled the rooms; he had fifty male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: His concubines filled the rooms, and he kept fifty male and female attendants.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相皆元功盛德，不務權威，出入騎從簡寡，士庶不甚引避。

translations.literal: By precedent, chancellors were men of founding merit and lofty virtue who did not pursue authority and majesty; going in and out their mounted retinues were simple and few, and scholars and commoners did not greatly shy away.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, chancellors were men of founding merit and lofty virtue who did not flaunt authority; their mounted retinues were modest, and scholars and commoners did not greatly shrink from their path.

sentences.zh: 林甫自見結怨者眾，憂刺客竊發，其出入，廣騶騎，先驅百步，傳呼何衛，金吾為清道，公卿辟易趨走。

translations.literal: Linfu himself saw that he had made many enemies and feared assassins might strike secretly; whenever he went out or in, he expanded his escort of mounted runners, with heralds a hundred paces ahead calling "Which guard?" The Golden Guard cleared the road, and nobles and ministers scattered and hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu knew he had made many enemies and feared a hidden assassin; whenever he went out, he expanded his mounted escort, with heralds a hundred paces ahead calling out which guard unit was passing. The Golden Guard cleared the road, and nobles and ministers scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 所居重關復壁，絡版甃石，一夕再徙，家人亦莫知也。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt had layered gates and double walls, latticed boards and piled stone; in a single night he would move twice, and even his household did not know.
translations.idiomatic: His residence had layered gates and double walls, latticed panels and piled stone; he would change sleeping quarters twice in a single night, and even his household did not know where he slept.

sentences.zh: 或帝不朝，群司要官悉走其門，臺省為空。

translations.literal: Sometimes when the Emperor did not hold court, key officials of all bureaus all rushed to his gate, and the central ministries stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when the Emperor did not hold court, key officials from every bureau flocked to Linfu's gate, and the central ministries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 左相陳希烈雖坐府，卒無人入謁。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Chen Xilie though seated in his office, in the end had no one come to pay calls.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Chen Xilie might sit in his office, but in the end no one came to pay calls.

sentences.zh: 林甫無學術，發言陋鄙，聞者竊笑。

translations.literal: Linfu had no learning; his utterances were coarse and vulgar, and listeners secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had no learning; his speech was coarse and vulgar, and those who heard him laughed behind his back.

sentences.zh: 善苑咸、郭慎微，使主書記。

translations.literal: He favored Yuan Xian and Guo Shenwei and had them manage clerical records.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Yuan Xian and Guo Shenwei and put them in charge of his correspondence.

sentences.zh: 然練文法，其用人非諂附者一以格令持之，故小小綱目不甚亂，而人憚其威權。

translations.literal: Yet he was practiced in statutes and regulations; in employing men he held all who were not sycophants strictly to the rules and precedents, so that minor regulations and details were not greatly chaotic, and people feared his awesome power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was well versed in statutes and regulations; in appointing men he held all who were not his sycophants strictly to the rules, so that minor affairs were not greatly disordered, and people feared his power.

sentences.zh: 久之，又兼安西大都護、朔方節度使。

translations.literal: After some time, he additionally served as Grand Protector of Anxi and Military Commissioner of Shuo-fang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he additionally served as Grand Protector of Anxi and Military Commissioner of Shuo-fang.

sentences.zh: 俄兼單于副大都護，以朔方副使李獻忠反，讓還節度。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally served as Vice Grand Protector of Shanyu; because Shuo-fang deputy commissioner Li Xianzhong rebelled, he returned the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he additionally served as Vice Grand Protector of Shanyu; when Shuo-fang deputy commissioner Li Xianzhong rebelled, he relinquished the military commission.

sentences.zh: 始厚王鉷，為盡力。

translations.literal: At first he treated Wang Hong generously and exerted himself on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: At first he treated Wang Hong generously and did everything he could for him.

sentences.zh: 及鉷敗，詔宰相治狀，林甫大懼，不敢面鉷，獄具署名，亦無所申救。

translations.literal: When Hong failed, the Emperor ordered the chancellors to investigate the case; Linfu was greatly afraid, dared not face Hong, and when the case was complete and signed, offered no plea to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong fell, the Emperor ordered the chancellors to investigate the case. Linfu was terrified, dared not face Hong, and when the indictment was complete and signed, made no effort to save him.

sentences.zh: 因以楊國忠代為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Guozhong was made to replace him as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Guozhong was appointed to replace him as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 林甫薄國忠材孱，無所畏，又以貴妃故善之。

translations.literal: Linfu looked down on Guozhong as weak in talent and felt no fear of him; moreover, because of the Noble Consort, he treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu despised Guozhong as a man of feeble ability and feared him not at all; yet because of the Noble Consort he remained on good terms with him.

sentences.zh: 及是權益盛，貴震天下，始交惡若仇敵。

translations.literal: By this time Guozhong's power grew ever stronger and his prestige shook the realm, and they began to hate each other like mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guozhong's power had grown overwhelming and his eminence shook the empire, and the two men came to hate each other like sworn foes.

sentences.zh: 然國忠方兼劍南節度使，而南蠻入寇，林甫因建遣之鎮，欲離間之。

translations.literal: But Guozhong was also serving as military commissioner of Jiannan, and when the southern barbarians raided, Linfu thereupon proposed sending him to take up his command there, intending to estrange him.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was also serving as military commissioner of Jiannan, and when the southern tribes raided the frontier, Linfu proposed dispatching him to take up his post there, hoping to drive a wedge between him and the court.

sentences.zh: 國忠入辭，帝曰：「處置且訖，亟還，指日待卿。」

translations.literal: Guozhong came to take leave; the Emperor said: 'Once matters are settled, return at once—I await you within days.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhong came to bid farewell, the Emperor said, 'Once affairs are handled, come back at once—I expect you within days.

sentences.zh: 林甫聞之憂懣。

translations.literal: When Linfu heard this he was distressed and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: When Linfu heard this, he was anguished and resentful.

sentences.zh: 是時已屬疾，稍侵。

translations.literal: At this time he was already ill, and the sickness was gradually worsening.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was already ill, and the disease was slowly spreading.

sentences.zh: 會帝幸溫湯，詔以馬輿從，禦醫珍膳繼至，詔旨存問，中官護起居。

translations.literal: When the Emperor happened to visit the hot springs, he decreed that Linfu should follow in a horse-litter; imperial physicians and fine food arrived in succession, edicts inquired after his health, and palace eunuchs attended his daily needs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited the hot springs, he ordered Linfu carried along in a horse-litter; imperial physicians and delicacies arrived one after another, edicts expressed concern for his condition, and palace eunuchs watched over his daily care.

sentences.zh: 病劇，巫者視疾云：「見天子當少間。」

translations.literal: When the illness grew severe, a shaman who examined his sickness said: 'If he sees the Son of Heaven he should recover somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: As the illness worsened, a shaman who divined his condition said, 'If he sees the Son of Heaven, he should improve somewhat.

sentences.zh: 帝欲視之，左右諫止。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to visit him, but those around him remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to visit him in person, but those at his side remonstrated and dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 乃詔林甫出廷中，帝登降聖閣，舉絳巾招之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Linfu to come out into the courtyard; the Emperor ascended the Jiangsheng Pavilion and waved a crimson kerchief to signal him.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Linfu out into the courtyard; the Emperor climbed the Jiangsheng Pavilion and waved a crimson kerchief to beckon him.

sentences.zh: 林甫不能興，左右代拜。

translations.literal: Linfu could not rise; those at his side bowed on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu could not get up; attendants at his side bowed in his place.

sentences.zh: 俄而國忠至自蜀，謁林甫床下，垂涕托後事，因不食卒。

translations.literal: Soon Guozhong arrived from Shu, called on Linfu at his bedside, wept and entrusted his affairs to him, and then died from refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guozhong returned from Shu, visited Linfu at his bedside, wept and entrusted his affairs to him, and then died from refusing all food.

sentences.zh: 諸子護還京發喪，贈太尉、揚州大都督。

translations.literal: His sons escorted the coffin back to the capital for the funeral; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor and Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons escorted the body back to the capital for the funeral; he was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Mentor and Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 林甫居相位凡十九年，固寵市權，蔽欺天子耳目，諫官皆持祿養資，無敢正言者。

translations.literal: Linfu held the chancellorship for nineteen years in all, entrenching favor and trading in power, obscuring and deceiving the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; remonstrating officials all merely held their salaries and nourished their resources, and none dared speak straight words.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu held the chancellorship for nineteen years in all, entrenching imperial favor and trading in power while screening and deceiving the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; remonstrating officials merely drew their salaries and kept their mouths shut, and none dared speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 補闕杜琎再上書言政事，斥為下邽令。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Supplementer Du Jin again submitted a memorial on state affairs and was dismissed to be magistrate of Xia Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Supplementer Du Jin again submitted a memorial on state affairs and was banished to serve as magistrate of Xia Gui.

sentences.zh: 因以語動其餘曰：「明主在上，群臣將順不暇，亦何所論？

translations.literal: Linfu thereupon used words to move the others, saying: 'An enlightened lord sits above; ministers scarcely have time to follow along—what is there to discuss?
translations.idiomatic: Linfu then used this case to warn the others, saying, 'An enlightened sovereign sits above us; ministers barely have time to fall in line—what is there left to debate?

sentences.zh: 君等獨不見立仗馬乎，終日無聲，而飫三品芻豆；

translations.literal: Do you not see the standing-ceremony horses? All day they make no sound, yet they are fed third-rank fodder and beans;
translations.idiomatic: Have you never seen the horses that stand in the palace guard ceremony? All day they make not a sound, yet they feast on third-rank fodder and beans;

sentences.zh: 一鳴，則黜之矣。

translations.literal: if one neighs, it is dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: if one neighs, it is cast out.

sentences.zh: 後雖欲不鳴，得乎？」

translations.literal: Later, even if it wished not to neigh, could it?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, even if it wished to stay silent, could it?

sentences.zh: 由是諫爭路絕。

translations.literal: From this the path of remonstrance and dispute was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, the road of remonstrance was closed entirely.

sentences.zh: 貞觀以來，任蕃將者如阿史那社爾、契何力皆以忠力奮，然猶不為上將，皆大臣總制之，故上有餘權以制於下。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenguan era, when foreign generals such as Ashina She'er and Qibi Heli were employed, they all exerted themselves with loyalty and strength, yet they were still not made supreme commanders—all were overseen by great ministers, so that the ruler above retained surplus authority to control those below.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguan era, foreign generals such as Ashina She'er and Qibi Heli had served with loyal zeal, yet even they were never made supreme commanders; great ministers always held overall command, so the throne retained enough leverage to keep subordinates in check.

sentences.zh: 先天、開元中，大臣若薛訥、郭元振、張嘉貞、王晙、張說、蕭嵩、杜暹、李適之等，自節度使入相天子。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian and Kaiyuan periods, great ministers such as Xue Ne, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Jiazhen, Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, Xiao Song, Du Xian, and Li Shizhi and others all entered the chancellorship from the post of military commissioner to serve the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian and Kaiyuan reigns, great ministers such as Xue Ne, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Jiazhen, Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, Xiao Song, Du Xian, and Li Shizhi had all risen from military commissioner to chancellor and served at the Son of Heaven's side.

sentences.zh: 林甫疾儒臣以方略積邊勞，且大任，欲杜其本，以久己權，即說帝曰：「以陛下雄材，國家富強，而夷狄未滅者，繇文吏為將，憚矢石，不身先。

translations.literal: Linfu resented that scholar-officials gained frontier merit through strategy and accumulated border achievements, and moreover received great appointments; wishing to cut off their root so as to prolong his own power, he thereupon said to the Emperor: 'With Your Majesty's heroic talent and the state's wealth and strength, the reason the barbarians of the Yi and Di are not yet destroyed is that civilian officials are made generals—they fear arrows and stones and do not lead from the front.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu resented scholar-officials who won frontier distinction through strategy, accumulated border achievements, and then received high office; wishing to cut off that path and prolong his own power, he told the Emperor, 'With Your Majesty's heroic gifts and the realm's wealth and strength, the reason the barbarians remain undefeated is that civilian officials are made generals—they dread arrows and stones and never lead the charge themselves.

sentences.zh: 不如用蕃將，彼生而雄，養馬上，長行陣，天性然也。

translations.literal: It would be better to use foreign generals—they are born fierce, reared on horseback, and grow up in battle formations; it is their nature.
translations.idiomatic: Better to use foreign generals—they are born fierce, raised in the saddle, and bred in battle lines; that is their nature.

sentences.zh: 若陛下感而用之，使必死，夷狄不足圖也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty moved by this employs them and makes them fight to the death, the Yi and Di barbarians need not be considered difficult to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wins them with kindness and puts them to use, making them fight to the death, the barbarians will be no great matter.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，因以安思順代林甫領節度，而擢安祿山、高仙芝、哥舒翰等專為大將。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed; thereupon An Sishun replaced Linfu in command of the military commission, while An Lushan, Gao Xianzhi, Geshu Han, and others were promoted to serve exclusively as great generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed. An Sishun replaced Linfu as military commissioner, while An Lushan, Gao Xianzhi, Geshu Han, and others were promoted to serve as great generals in their own right.

sentences.zh: 林甫利其虜也，無入相之資，故祿山得專三道勁兵，處十四年不徙，天子安林甫策，不疑也，卒稱兵蕩覆天下，王室遂微。

translations.literal: Linfu took advantage of the fact that they were barbarians and lacked qualifications to enter the chancellorship, so Lushan was able to hold sole command over three circuits' crack troops and remain in place fourteen years without transfer; the Son of Heaven rested secure in Linfu's policy and harbored no suspicion, until Lushan finally raised arms, overturned and devastated the realm, and the royal house then declined.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu counted on the fact that they were barbarians with no prospect of entering the chancellorship, so Lushan was left in sole command of crack troops across three circuits for fourteen years without transfer; the Son of Heaven trusted Linfu's policy and suspected nothing—until Lushan finally raised arms, overturned the realm, and the royal house withered.

sentences.zh: 初，林甫夢人皙而髯，將逼己。

translations.literal: Earlier, Linfu dreamed of a man fair-skinned and bearded who was about to press upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Linfu had dreamed of a fair-skinned, bearded man closing in on him.

sentences.zh: 寤而物色，得裴寬類所夢，曰：「寬欲代我。」

translations.literal: Awaking, he searched for such a person and found Pei Kuan resembled the one in the dream; he said, 'Kuan wishes to replace me.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he searched for such a man and found that Pei Kuan matched the dream; he said, 'Kuan means to take my place.

sentences.zh: 因李適之黨逐之。

translations.literal: Through Li Shizhi's faction he had him driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Through Li Shizhi's faction he had Kuan driven out.

sentences.zh: 其後楊國忠代林甫，貌類寬雲。

translations.literal: Later Yang Guozhong replaced Linfu, and his appearance resembled Kuan's—they said so.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Guozhong replaced Linfu—and his appearance matched Kuan's, just as the omen had foretold.

sentences.zh: 國忠素銜林甫，及未葬，陰諷祿山暴其短。

translations.literal: Guozhong had long harbored resentment against Linfu, and before he was even buried, secretly incited Lushan to expose his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong had long resented Linfu, and before the body was even buried he secretly urged Lushan to expose Linfu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 祿山使阿布思降將入朝，告林甫與思約為父子，有異謀。

translations.literal: Lushan sent the surrendered general Abu Si to court to report that Linfu and Si had sworn brotherhood as father and son and had a treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent the surrendered general Abu Si to court to accuse Linfu of having sworn a pact of father and son with Si and plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 事下有司，其婿楊齊宣懼，妄言林甫厭祝上，國忠劾其奸。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the relevant offices; his son-in-law Yang Qixuan, in fear, falsely claimed Linfu had used curses and sorcery against the Emperor, and Guozhong impeached him for treachery.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the proper offices; his son-in-law Yang Qixuan, terrified, falsely claimed that Linfu had cursed the Emperor with sorcery, and Guozhong impeached him for treason.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔林甫淫祀厭勝，結叛虜，圖危宗社，悉奪官爵，斫棺剔取含珠金紫，更以小槥，用庶人禮葬之；

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and decreed that Linfu had practiced improper sacrifices and curse-magic, conspired with rebellious barbarians, and plotted to endanger the altars of state; all his titles were stripped, his coffin was hacked open and the pearl in his mouth and gold and purple regalia removed, he was re-coffined in a small coffin, and buried with commoner's rites;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and decreed that Linfu had practiced illicit sacrifices and curse-magic, conspired with rebel barbarians, and plotted against the altars of state; all his titles were stripped, his coffin was hacked open and the mouth-pearl and gold and purple vestments removed, he was re-coffined in a small box, and buried with commoner's rites;

sentences.zh: 諸子司儲郎中、太常少卿嶼及岫等悉徙嶺南、黔中，各給奴婢三人，籍其家；

translations.literal: His sons—Director of Palace Provision Yu, Vice Director of Court Ceremonies Yu and Xiu and the others—were all exiled to Lingnan and Qianzhong, each given three slaves, and their households were confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: His sons—Director of Palace Provision Yu, Vice Director of Court Ceremonies Yu, Xiu, and the rest—were all exiled to Lingnan and Qianzhong, each given three slaves, and their property was confiscated;

sentences.zh: 諸婿若張博濟、鄭平、杜位、元撝，屬子復道、光，皆貶官。

translations.literal: All the sons-in-law—Zhang Boji, Zheng Ping, Du Wei, Yuan Hui—and subordinate sons Fudao and Guang were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons-in-law—Zhang Boji, Zheng Ping, Du Wei, and Yuan Hui—and his younger sons Fudao and Guang were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 博濟亦憸薄自肆。

translations.literal: Boji was likewise treacherous and frivolous, indulging himself freely.
translations.idiomatic: Boji was likewise cunning, shallow, and utterly unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 為戶部郎中，部有考堂，天下歲會計處，博濟廢為員外郎中聽事，壯偉華敞，供擬豐侈至千品；

translations.literal: As a director in the Ministry of Revenue—the ministry had an examination hall where the empire's annual accounts were gathered—Boji converted it into the reception office of an auxiliary director; it was grand, splendid, and spacious, with provisions and furnishings lavish to a thousand kinds;
translations.idiomatic: As a director in the Ministry of Revenue—whose examination hall was where the empire's annual accounts were compiled—Boji turned it into the reception office of an auxiliary director; the building was grand and lavish, with provisions and furnishings running to a thousand items;

sentences.zh: 別取都水監地為考堂，擅費諸州籍帳錢不貲，有司不敢言。

translations.literal: He separately seized land from the Directorate of Waterways for an examination hall and squandered without limit the registry-account funds of the various prefectures; the relevant offices dared not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He separately seized land from the Directorate of Waterways for a new examination hall and recklessly spent the registry funds of the prefectures without restraint; the responsible offices dared not protest.

sentences.zh: 帝之幸蜀也，給事中裴士淹以辯學得幸。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fled to Shu, Supervising Secretary Pei Shiyan won favor through eloquence and learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fled to Shu, Supervising Secretary Pei Shiyan won favor through his eloquence and erudition.

sentences.zh: 時肅宗在鳳翔，每命宰相，輒啟聞。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Suzong was at Fengxiang; whenever he appointed a chancellor he always reported to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Suzong was at Fengxiang; whenever he appointed a chancellor he always sent word to inform the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 及房琯為將，帝曰：「此非破賊才也。

translations.literal: When Fang Guan was made a general, the Emperor said: 'This is not talent for breaking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guan was made a general, the Emperor said, 'He is not the man to break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 若姚元崇在，賊不足滅。」

translations.literal: If Yao Chong were alive, the rebels would not be worth the trouble of destroying.
translations.idiomatic: If Yao Chong were still alive, the rebels would scarcely be worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 至宋璟，曰：「彼賣直以取名耳。」

translations.literal: As for Song Jing, he said: 'That man sold integrity to win a reputation.'
translations.idiomatic: Of Song Jing he said, 'That man sold his integrity to buy a reputation.'

sentences.zh: 因歷評十餘人，皆當。

translations.literal: He then went through more than ten men in turn, appraising each, and all his judgments were apt.
translations.idiomatic: He then ran through more than ten men in succession, and every judgment hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 至林甫，曰：「是子妒賢疾能，舉無比者。」

translations.literal: When it came to Linfu, he said: 'That man is jealous of the worthy and hates the able—none can compare with him in this.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to Linfu, he said, 'That man is jealous of the worthy and hates the able—there is no equal to him in that.

sentences.zh: 士淹因曰：「陛下誠知之，何任之久邪？」

translations.literal: Shiyan thereupon said: 'If Your Majesty truly knows this, why employ him so long?'
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan then said, 'If Your Majesty truly knows this, why keep him in office so long?'

sentences.zh: 帝默不應。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 至德中，兩京平，大赦，唯祿山支黨及林甫、楊國忠、王鉷子孫不原。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era, when the two capitals were recovered, a general amnesty was proclaimed, but only the Lushan faction and the descendants of Linfu, Yang Guozhong, and Wang Hong were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era, after the two capitals were recovered, a general amnesty was proclaimed—but the Lushan faction and the descendants of Linfu, Yang Guozhong, and Wang Hong alone were excluded.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，嘗鏤玉為玄元皇帝及玄宗、肅宗像於太清宮，復琢林甫、陳希烈像列左右序。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period they once carved jade images of the Emperor Xuanyuan and of Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong at the Taiqing Palace, and also carved images of Linfu and Chen Xilie to stand in ranks to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao period jade images of the Emperor Xuanyuan, of Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong, and also of Linfu and Chen Xilie were carved for the Taiqing Palace and arranged in order to left and right.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，或言：「林甫陰險，嘗不利先帝，宗廟幾危，奈何留像至今？」

translations.literal: In Emperor Daizong's time, someone said: 'Linfu was sinister and crafty; he once harmed the Former Emperor, and the imperial ancestral temple was nearly endangered—why keep his image until now?
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Daizong's reign someone said, 'Linfu was treacherous and once harmed the Former Emperor; the ancestral temple was nearly lost—why does his image remain?

sentences.zh: 有詔瘞宮中。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to bury it within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it buried within the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，盧攜為太清宮使，發地得其像，輦送京兆毀之云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangming era, Lu Xie was commissioner of the Taiqing Palace; excavating the ground he recovered the image, had it carted to the capital prefecture to be destroyed, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangming era, Lu Xie was commissioner of the Taiqing Palace; when the ground was dug up the image was found, carted to the capital prefecture, and destroyed—or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈者，宋州人。

translations.literal: Chen Xilie was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie was a native of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 博學，尤深黃老，工文章。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he was especially deep in the teachings of Huang-Lao and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned, especially steeped in Huang-Lao thought, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 開元中，帝儲思經義，自褚無量、元行沖卒，而希烈與康子元、馮朝隱進講禁中，其應答詔問，敷盡微隱，皆希烈為之章句。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period the Emperor in his leisure pondered the meaning of the classics; after Chu Wuliang and Yuan Xingchong died, Xilie together with Kang Ziyuan and Feng Chaoyin lectured within the palace; in answering imperial questions and setting forth hidden subtleties to the full, Xilie prepared all the commentarial passages.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign the Emperor, in his leisure, pondered the meaning of the classics; after Chu Wuliang and Yuan Xingchong died, Xilie lectured in the inner palace with Kang Ziyuan and Feng Chaoyin, and whenever the Emperor questioned him and hidden subtleties had to be fully expounded, Xilie supplied all the commentarial passages.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，十九年為集賢院學士，進工部侍郎，知院事。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Drafting Secretary; in the nineteenth year he became an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was promoted to Vice Minister of Public Works, and directed the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to Drafting Secretary; in the nineteenth year he became an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was promoted to Vice Minister of Public Works, and directed the academy.

sentences.zh: 帝有所撰述，希烈必助成之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor undertook any composition, Xilie always assisted in completing it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor undertook a literary project, Xilie always helped bring it to completion.

sentences.zh: 遷門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，有神降丹鳳門，以為老子告錫靈符，希烈因是上言：「臣侍演《南華真經》至七篇，陛下顧曰：『此言養生，朕既悟其術，而《德充符》詎無非常應哉？』

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao a spirit descended at Danfeng Gate; it was taken as Laozi announcing the bestowal of a numinous talisman. Xilie thereupon submitted a memorial: 'Your servant was lecturing on the Zhuangzi through the seventh chapter when Your Majesty turned and said, "This speaks of nourishing life—I have already grasped its art; yet surely the chapter Sign of Complete Virtue should have some extraordinary response, should it not?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao a spirit descended at Danfeng Gate, taken as Laozi announcing the gift of a numinous talisman. Xilie thereupon memorialized: 'While Your servant was lecturing on the Zhuangzi through the seventh chapter, Your Majesty turned and said, "This speaks of nurturing life—I have already grasped its method; yet surely the chapter Sign of Complete Virtue ought to have some extraordinary response, should it not?

sentences.zh: 臣稽首對：『陛下德充於內，符應於外，必有絕瑞表之。』

translations.literal: Your servant bowed head to ground and replied: 'Your Majesty's virtue is complete within, and signs respond without—there must be a supreme auspice to manifest it.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bowed and replied, 'Your Majesty's virtue is complete within, and signs respond without—there must be a supreme omen to reveal it.'

sentences.zh: 今靈符降錫，與帝意合，宜示史官，著顯祥，摛照無窮。」

translations.literal: Now the numinous talisman has descended and been granted—it accords with the Emperor's thought. It should be shown to the historiographers, recorded as a brilliant omen, and its radiance displayed without end."
translations.idiomatic: Now the numinous talisman has descended in accord with the Emperor's thought. It should be shown to the historiographers, recorded as a brilliant omen, and its radiance proclaimed without end."

sentences.zh: 其俞佞類如此。

translations.literal: His sycophantic flattery was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His sycophantic flattery ran to such lengths.

sentences.zh: 俄兼崇玄館大學士，封臨潁侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Grand Academician of the Palace of Venerating the Mysteries and enfeoffed as Marquis of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Grand Academician of the Palace of Venerating the Mysteries and enfeoffed as Marquis of Linying.

sentences.zh: 林甫顓朝，茍用可專制者，引與共政。

translations.literal: Linfu monopolized the court; any servile man who could be used for sole control, he drew in to share government.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu monopolized the court; any pliable man he could use to rule alone, he brought in to share power.

sentences.zh: 以希烈柔易，且帝眷之厚，乃薦之。

translations.literal: Because Xilie was gentle and tractable and moreover enjoyed the Emperor's thick favor, Linfu recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xilie was mild and compliant and enjoyed the Emperor's deep favor, Linfu recommended him.

sentences.zh: 五載，進同中書門下平章事，遷左丞相兼兵部尚書，許國公，又兼秘書省圖書使，寵與林甫侔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery and given equal rank as Grand Counselor, transferred to Left Grand Counselor together with Minister of War, made Duke of Xu, and additionally made commissioner of the Palace Library's books; his favor rivaled Linfu's.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery with equal rank as Grand Counselor, made Left Grand Counselor and Minister of War, enfeoffed as Duke of Xu, and additionally appointed commissioner of the Palace Library—his favor rivaled Linfu's.

sentences.zh: 林甫居位久，其陰詭雖足自固，亦希烈左右焉。

translations.literal: Linfu had long held his post; though his covert schemes were sufficient to secure himself, he also relied on Xilie at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had long held office; though his secret machinations were enough to secure himself, he also leaned on Xilie at his side.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠執政，素忌之，希烈引避，國忠即薦韋見素代相，罷為太子太師。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong held power he had long envied him; Xilie withdrew to avoid him, and Guozhong immediately recommended Wei Jiansu to replace him as chancellor; Xilie was demoted to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong took power he had long envied Xilie; Xilie withdrew to avoid him, and Guozhong immediately recommended Wei Jiansu to replace him as chancellor, demoting Xilie to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 希烈失職，內忽忽無所賴。

translations.literal: Stripped of office, Xilie inwardly grew restless, with nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of office, Xilie grew inwardly restless, with nothing left to lean on.

sentences.zh: 及祿山盜京師，遂與達奚珣等偕相賊。

translations.literal: When Lushan seized the capital, he thereupon served jointly as chancellor for the rebels together with Daxi Xun and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan seized the capital, he joined Daxi Xun and others in serving the rebels as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 後論罪當斬，肅宗以上皇素所遇，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Later, when guilt was assessed and execution was called for, Suzong, because the Retired Emperor had always favored him, granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when guilt was assessed and execution was warranted, Suzong, because the Retired Emperor had always favored him, granted him death at home.

sentences.zh: ◎奸臣下盧杞盧杞，字子良。

translations.literal: ◎ Corrupt Officials (Lower): Lu Qi. Lu Qi, courtesy name Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Corrupt Officials (Lower) — Lu Qi. Lu Qi, whose courtesy name was Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 父弈，見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: His father Yi—see the Biographies of Loyal Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi—see the Biographies of Loyal Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 杞有口才，體陋甚，鬼貌藍色，不恥惡衣菲食，人未悟其不情，咸謂有祖風節。

translations.literal: Qi had a gift for speech, but his build was extremely ugly—his face was ghostlike and bluish; he was not ashamed of coarse clothes and meager food, and before people realized how ruthless he was, all said he had his grandfather's integrity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was eloquent, but his body was grotesquely ugly—his face ghostly and bluish; he wore coarse clothes and ate plain food without shame, and before anyone saw through his cold heart, all said he had inherited his grandfather's integrity.

sentences.zh: 藉蔭為清道率府兵曹參軍，仆固懷恩辟朔方府掌書記，病免。

translations.literal: Through inherited privilege he became Army Staff Officer of the Qingdao Leading Office; Pugu Huai'en recruited him as secretary of the Shuofang headquarters, but he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Through inherited privilege he became army staff officer of the Qingdao Leading Office; Pugu Huai'en recruited him as secretary of the Shuofang headquarters, but he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 補鴻臚丞，出為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide of the Court of State Ceremonial and sent out as prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide of the Court of State Ceremonial and sent out as prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 上謁節度府衛伯玉，伯玉不喜，乃謝歸。

translations.literal: He went up to call on Military Commissioner Wei Boyu at his headquarters; Boyu took no liking to him, and he thereupon excused himself and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He went to call on Military Commissioner Wei Boyu; Boyu took no liking to him, and Qi excused himself and returned.

sentences.zh: 稍遷吏部郎中，為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel and served as prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel and appointed prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 奏言虢有官豕三千為民患。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Guo had three thousand official pigs that were a pest to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Guo had three thousand official pigs that were plaguing the people.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「徙之沙苑。」

translations.literal: Dezong said: 'Move them to Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, 'Move them to Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 杞曰：「同州亦陛下百姓，臣謂食之便。」

translations.literal: Qi said: 'The people of Tongzhou are also Your Majesty's commoners; Your servant thinks it would be better to have them eaten.'
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, 'The people of Tongzhou are also Your Majesty's subjects; Your servant thinks it would be better to have the pigs eaten.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「守虢而憂它州，宰相材也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'To hold Guo yet worry about other prefectures—that is chancellor material.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'To govern Guo yet worry about other prefectures—that is the mark of a chancellor.'

sentences.zh: 詔以豕賜貧民，遂有意柄任矣。

translations.literal: An edict granted the pigs to the poor, and from then on he was marked for high office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the pigs to the poor, and from then on the Emperor marked him for high office.

sentences.zh: 俄召為御史中丞，論奏無不合。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief; his prosecutions and memorials never failed to accord with the Emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief; his indictments and memorials never failed to please the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 逾年遷大夫，不閱旬，擢門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Within a year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; in less than ten days he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-signer with equal rank as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was made Censor-in-Chief; in less than ten days he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-signer with equal rank as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 既得誌，險賊浸露。

translations.literal: Once he had attained his ambition, his malicious villainy gradually showed itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had gained his aim, his treacherous cruelty gradually emerged.

sentences.zh: 賢者冒，能者忌，小忤己，不傅死地不止。

translations.literal: He encroached on the worthy and envied the capable; for the slightest offense against himself he would not stop until they reached death's door.
translations.idiomatic: He encroached on the worthy and envied the capable; for the smallest slight he would not rest until his victim stood at death's door.

sentences.zh: 將大樹威，脅眾市權為自固者。

translations.literal: Intending to raise great authority, he intimidated the multitude and traded in power to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on building towering authority, he intimidated the court and traded in power to fortify his position.

sentences.zh: 楊炎與杞俱輔政，炎鄙杞才下，不悅，未半歲，譖罷炎。

translations.literal: Yang Yan and Qi served together as assistants in government; Yan looked down on Qi's inferior talent and was displeased; within half a year Qi slandered him and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan served alongside Qi as chancellor; Yan despised Qi's lesser ability and disliked him; within half a year Qi slandered him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 時大理卿嚴郢與炎有隙，即擢郢御史大夫以自助，炎卒逐死。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yan Yi bore a grudge against Yan; Qi immediately promoted Yi to Censor-in-Chief to bolster himself, and Yan in the end was driven out and died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yan Yi bore a grudge against Yang Yan; Qi immediately promoted Yi to Censor-in-Chief to bolster himself, and Yang Yan was ultimately driven out and died.

sentences.zh: 張鎰材裕忠懿，帝所倚愛，未有以間。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was talented, generous, loyal, and virtuous; the Emperor relied on and favored him, and there had been no opening to get at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was talented, generous, loyal, and upright; the Emperor relied on and favored him, and Qi had found no opening against him.

sentences.zh: 會隴右用兵，杞乃見帝，偽請行，帝不可，即薦鎰守鳳翔。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed in Longyou, Qi then appeared before the Emperor and falsely volunteered to go himself; when the Emperor refused, he immediately recommended Yi to guard Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were mobilized in Longyou, Qi appeared before the Emperor and falsely offered to go in person; when the Emperor refused, he immediately recommended Zhang Yi to guard Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 既又惡郢。

translations.literal: Soon he also hated Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also turned against Yan Yi.

sentences.zh: 時幽州朱滔與泚有違言，誣其軍司馬蔡廷玉間鬩，請殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao of Youzhou had a falling-out with Ci and falsely accused his army vice director Cai Tingyu of sowing discord, requesting that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Tao of Youzhou had fallen out with Zhu Ci and falsely accused Ci's army vice director Cai Tingyu of sowing discord, requesting his execution.

sentences.zh: 俄而滔反，帝欲斥之以悅滔，下御史鄭詹按狀，貶柳州司戶參軍，敕吏護送。

translations.literal: Soon Tao rebelled; the Emperor wished to banish someone to please Tao, so the matter was sent to Censor Zheng Zhan to investigate; Tingyu was demoted to army staff officer of Liuzhou, with orders for officials to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tao rebelled; the Emperor wished to banish someone to appease him, so Censor Zheng Zhan was ordered to investigate; Tingyu was demoted to army staff officer of Liuzhou and officials were commanded to escort him.

sentences.zh: 廷玉疑送滔所，因自沈於河。

translations.literal: Tingyu suspected he was being sent to Tao's territory and therefore drowned himself in a river.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu suspected he was being sent into Tao's hands and drowned himself in a river.

sentences.zh: 杞奏，恐泚疑為詔所殺，願下詹三司雜治，並劾大夫郢。

translations.literal: Qi memorialized that he feared Ci would suspect Tingyu had been killed by imperial order; he wished to have Zhan turned over to the Three Offices for joint trial, and simultaneously impeach Censor-in-Chief Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi memorialized that he feared Ci would suspect Tingyu had been killed by imperial order; he asked that Zhan be turned over to the Three Offices for joint trial and simultaneously impeached Censor-in-Chief Yan Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，詹善張鎰，每伺杞間，獨詣鎰，杞知之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan had been on good terms with Zhang Yi; whenever he spied an opening while Qi was occupied, he would visit Yi alone—and Qi knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhan had been on good terms with Zhang Yi; whenever he found an opening while Qi was occupied, he would visit Yi alone—and Qi knew it.

sentences.zh: 它日伺詹來，即徑至鎰便坐。

translations.literal: Another day, watching for Zhan's arrival, he went straight to Yi's informal seat.
translations.idiomatic: One day, having watched for Zhan's visit, Qi went straight to where Yi was sitting informally.

sentences.zh: 詹趨避，杞遽及機事，鎰不得已，曰：「鄭侍禦在。」

translations.literal: Zhan hurried to avoid him; Qi immediately raised the confidential matter. Yi had no choice but to say: 'Investigating Censor Zheng is here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan rushed to slip away, but Qi at once pressed the sensitive business. Yi could only say, "Investigating Censor Zheng is here.

sentences.zh: 杞陽驚曰：「向所言，非外所得聞。」

translations.literal: Qi feigned surprise and said: 'What was said earlier could not have been heard from outside.'
translations.idiomatic: Qi pretended to be startled. "What we were discussing could not have been overheard from outside," he said.

sentences.zh: 至是並按。

translations.literal: At this both were investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were then investigated together.

sentences.zh: 有詔詹杖死，流郢費州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhan beaten to death and Yan exiled to Feizhou in Ying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Zhan beaten to death and sent Yan Yi into exile at Feizhou in Ying.

sentences.zh: 杜佑判度支，帝尤寵禮。

translations.literal: Du You served as acting head of the Revenue Bureau; the Emperor especially favored and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was acting head of the Revenue Bureau, and the Emperor treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 杞短毀百緒，訖貶蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: Qi slandered him on countless points until he was demoted to prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi picked fault with him on endless pretexts until he was demoted to prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 李希烈反，杞素惡顏真卿挺正敢言，即令宣慰其軍，卒為賊害。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, Qi had long resented Yan Zhenqing's upright candor; he immediately sent him to pacify Xilie's army, and he was ultimately harmed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, Qi—who had long resented Yan Zhenqing's upright outspokenness—sent him to pacify Xilie's forces, and Yan was ultimately killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 故宰相李揆有雅望，畏復用，遣為吐蕃會盟使，卒於行。

translations.literal: The former chancellor Li Kui enjoyed high repute; fearing he might be reemployed, Qi sent him as envoy to the Tibetan alliance conference, and he died on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The former chancellor Li Kui enjoyed great prestige. Fearing he might be brought back into office, Qi dispatched him as envoy to a treaty conference with Tibet, and Li died on the road.

sentences.zh: 李洧以徐州降，有所經略，使人誤先白鎰，杞怒，沮解之，不使有功。

translations.literal: When Li Xu surrendered Xuzhou, he had plans in mind; a messenger mistakenly reported first to Yi. Qi was angry, obstructed and dissolved the arrangements, and kept Xu from achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xu surrendered Xuzhou he had strategic plans in hand, but a messenger mistakenly reported to Zhang Yi first. Qi was furious, blocked and unraveled the operation, and kept Xu from winning any credit.

sentences.zh: 其狙害隱毒，天下無不痛憤，以杞得君，故不敢言。

translations.literal: His lurking injuries and hidden poison—there was no one under Heaven who did not feel pain and rage; because Qi held the Emperor's favor, they dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His ambushes and hidden malice left the whole empire aching with outrage, yet because Qi held the sovereign's ear, no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 是時兵屯河南、北，挐不解，財用日急。

translations.literal: At this time armies were stationed north and south of the Yellow River, locked in stalemate without release, and finances grew daily more pressing.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were then encamped north and south of the Yellow River in a grip that would not loosen, and the treasury grew tighter by the day.

sentences.zh: 於是度支條軍所仰給，月費緡百餘萬，而藏錢才支三月。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Revenue Bureau itemized what the armies depended upon for supply: monthly expenditure exceeded a million strings of cash, while stored funds could support only three months.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Bureau then tallied what the armies required: more than a million strings of cash each month, while reserves would last only three months.

sentences.zh: 杞乃以戶部侍郎趙贊判度支，其黨韋都賓等建言：「商賈儲錢千萬，聽自業；

translations.literal: Qi then had Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan act as head of the Revenue Bureau; his clique—Wei Dubin and others—proposed: 'Merchants who store ten million in cash may keep their own business;
translations.idiomatic: Qi put Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan in charge of the bureau, and his allies Wei Dubin and others proposed: "Merchants who hoard ten million in cash may keep trading as they please;

sentences.zh: 過千萬者，貣其贏以濟軍。

translations.literal: Those exceeding ten million shall lend their surplus profits to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: those who hold more than ten million must lend their surplus profits to support the army.

sentences.zh: 軍罷，約取償於官。」

translations.literal: When the armies stand down, repayment from the government is stipulated.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaigns end, the government will repay them as agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 京兆暴責其期，校吏頸大搜廛裏，疑占列不盡，則笞掠之，人不勝冤，自殞溝瀆者相望，京師囂然不闋日。

translations.literal: The metropolitan prefecture violently enforced the deadline; clerks with measuring chains on their necks searched throughout the market district; those suspected of underreporting were flogged and tortured. People unable to bear the injustice threw themselves into ditches and streams in unbroken succession; the capital seethed without a day's quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan prefecture enforced the deadline with brutal haste. Clerks wearing measuring chains on their necks ransacked the markets; anyone suspected of concealing holdings was beaten and tortured. Desperate people drowned themselves in ditches and streams in an unbroken line, and the capital roared with protest day after day.

sentences.zh: 然悉田宅奴婢之直，緡止八十萬。

translations.literal: Yet counting the full value of fields, houses, slaves, and servants, they raised only eight hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even after seizing the full value of fields, houses, slaves, and servants, they collected only eight hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 又僦櫝、質舍、居貿粟者，四貣其一，僅至二百萬。

translations.literal: When they also levied on rented coffers, pawnshops, and grain merchants in residence, taking one quarter from each, they reached only two million.
translations.idiomatic: When they also assessed rented strongboxes, pawnshops, and grain dealers, taking one quarter from each, the total rose to only two million.

sentences.zh: 而長安為閉肆，民皆邀宰相祈訴。

translations.literal: Yet Chang'an shut its shops, and the people all waylaid the chancellors to plead for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an closed its shops anyway, and commoners waylaid the chancellors in the streets to beg for mercy.

sentences.zh: 杞無以諭，驅而去。

translations.literal: Qi had no way to persuade them and had them driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Qi could not reason with them and had them driven away.

sentences.zh: 帝知民愁忿，而所得不足給師，罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew the people were aggrieved and angry, but the proceeds were insufficient to supply the armies, so the measure was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the people's fury, but the yield was too small to feed the armies, and the scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 贊術窮，於是間架、除陌之暴縱矣。

translations.literal: Zhan's schemes exhausted, thereupon the ruthless imposition of the jianjia and chumo taxes followed.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhao Zan's methods exhausted, the brutal jianjia and chumo taxes were unleashed next.

sentences.zh: 其法：屋二架為間，差稅之，上者二千，中千，下五百，吏執籌入第室計之，隱不盡，率二架抵罪，告者以錢五萬畀之。

translations.literal: The law: two rafters' width of a house counted as one bay; graduated taxes were imposed—upper grade two thousand, middle one thousand, lower five hundred. Officials carrying tally-sticks entered houses and counted; concealing anything was punished by two bays' worth of charges; informers received fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, every two rafters counted as one bay and was taxed by grade—two thousand for the highest, one thousand for the middle, five hundred for the lowest. Officials with tally-sticks entered homes to measure; anyone who concealed space paid a penalty of two bays, and informers received fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 凡公私貿易，舊法率千錢算二十，請加五十，主儈註所售，入其算有司；

translations.literal: For all public and private trade, the old law levied twenty per thousand cash; they requested adding fifty; the chief broker registered what was sold and submitted the reckoning to the relevant office;
translations.idiomatic: On all public and private trade the old rate had been twenty per thousand cash; they asked to add fifty. The chief broker recorded each sale and reported the tally to the authorities;

sentences.zh: 其自相市，為私籍自言，隱不盡，率千錢沒二萬，告者以萬錢畀之。

translations.literal: When parties traded among themselves, they were to keep private registers and report voluntarily; concealing anything incurred confiscation of twenty thousand per thousand concealed; informers received ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: when buyers and sellers dealt directly with one another they were to keep private ledgers and declare the amounts themselves. Concealment brought confiscation of twenty thousand for every thousand hidden, and informers received ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 由是主儈得操其私以為奸，公上所入常不得半，而恨誹之聲滿天下。

translations.literal: Thus chief brokers could wield private power to commit fraud; the government seldom received even half, while hatred and derision filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chief brokers thus wielded private leverage for fraud; the treasury rarely saw even half the due revenue, and resentment and ridicule spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 及涇師亂，呼於市曰：「不奪而商人僦質矣，不稅而間架、除陌矣！」

translations.literal: When the Jingshi troops mutinied, they shouted in the market: 'Without confiscation the merchants were squeezed for loans and pawn! Without taxation came the jianjia and chumo levies!
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingshi troops rebelled, they cried in the markets: "They did not seize our goods, yet merchants were squeezed for loans and pawn! They did not tax us, yet jianjia and chumo were imposed!

sentences.zh: 其倡和造作以召怨挻亂，皆杞為之。

translations.literal: The incitement and agitation that summoned resentment and spread disorder were all Qi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The slogans that stirred hatred and spread chaos were all Qi's work.

sentences.zh: 帝出奉天，杞與關播從。

translations.literal: The Emperor fled to Fengtian; Qi and Guan Bo followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor escaped to Fengtian, with Qi and Guan Bo in attendance.

sentences.zh: 後數日，崔寧自賊中來，以播遷事指杞，杞即誣寧反，帝殺之。

translations.literal: Several days later Cui Ning came from among the rebels and, regarding the court's flight, pointed at Qi; Qi immediately accused Ning of rebellion, and the Emperor had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Cui Ning arrived from rebel-held territory and, speaking of the court's flight, implicated Qi. Qi at once accused Ning of treason, and the Emperor had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 靈武杜希全率鹽、夏二州士六千來赴，帝議所從道，杞請道漠谷。

translations.literal: Du Xiquan of Lingwu led six thousand men from Yan and Xia prefectures to come to the rescue; the Emperor debated which route to take, and Qi requested the Mogu pass road.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan of Lingwu led six thousand troops from Yan and Xia to the rescue. When the court debated which route to take, Qi urged the Mogu pass.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊曰：「不然，彼多險，且為賊乘，不如道乾陵北，逾雞子堆而屯，與為掎角，賊可破矣。」

translations.literal: Hun Jian said: 'Not so—that route is full of peril and will give the rebels an opening; better to take the road north of Qianling, cross over Jizi Ridge and encamp, forming pincers with them—the rebels can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian said, "No—that way is treacherous and gives the rebels their chance. Better to march north of Qianling, cross Jizi Ridge, and encamp in pincers with our allies. Then the rebels can be broken.

sentences.zh: 帝從杞議，賊果拒隘，兵不得入，奔還邠州。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed Qi's plan; the rebels indeed blocked the narrows, the troops could not enter, and they fled back to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sided with Qi. The rebels held the defiles as expected, the army could not pass, and the force retreated to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 李懷光自河北還，數破賊，泚解去。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang returned from Hebei, repeatedly defeated the rebels, and Zhu Ci lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang marched back from Hebei, routed the rebels again and again, and Zhu Ci broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或謂王翃、趙贊曰：「聞懷光嘗斥宰相不能謀，度支賦斂重，而京兆刻損軍賜，宜誅之以謝天下。

translations.literal: Someone said to Wang Hong and Zhao Zan: 'I hear Huai'guang has denounced the chancellors for incompetence, the Revenue Bureau for heavy levies, and the metropolitan prefecture for cutting army rewards—Qi and company ought to be executed to appease the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Wang Hong and Zhao Zan, "I hear Huai'guang has blasted the chancellors for bad counsel, the Revenue Bureau for crushing taxes, and the metropolitan office for skimming army pay. Qi and his circle ought to be executed to satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 方懷光有功，上必聽用其言，公等殆矣！」

translations.literal: Huai'guang has just rendered great service; the Emperor is sure to heed him—you gentlemen are in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang has just saved the dynasty. The Emperor will surely listen to him—and you gentlemen are finished!

sentences.zh: 二人以白杞。

translations.literal: The two men reported this to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The two reported this to Qi.

sentences.zh: 杞懼，即譎帝曰：「懷光勛在宗社，賊憚之破膽，今因其威，可一舉而定。

translations.literal: Qi feared this and immediately deceived the Emperor, saying: 'Huai'guang's merit lies in saving the dynasty; the rebels fear him to the point of terror. Now by riding his prestige we can settle matters in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was terrified and at once misled the Emperor: "Huai'guang's service has saved the dynasty; the rebels are terrified of him. If we ride that momentum, we can finish this in one blow.

sentences.zh: 若許來朝，則犒賜留連，賊得裒整殘餘為完守計，圖之實難，不如席勝使平京師，破竹之勢也。」

translations.literal: If we allow him to come to court, rewards and banquets will detain him, and the rebels will gather their scattered remnants and plan a complete defense—attacking them will truly be hard. Better to strike while victory is hot and have him pacify the capital—the momentum of splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: If he is allowed to come to court, feasts and rewards will delay him while the rebels regroup and fortify the capital. Then the campaign will be hard indeed. Better to strike while the iron is hot and let him sweep Chang'an—the way bamboo splits once the first joint gives.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔懷光無朝，進屯便橋。

translations.literal: An edict forbade Huai'guang from coming to court and ordered him to advance and encamp at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict barred Huai'guang from audience and ordered him to press forward and camp at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 懷光自以千里勤難，有大功，為奸臣沮間，不一見天子，內怏怏無所發，遂謀反，因暴言杞等罪惡。

translations.literal: Huai'guang considered that he had rushed a thousand li to save the dynasty in crisis and won great merit, yet wicked ministers obstructed and alienated him, denying him even one audience with the Son of Heaven. Inwardly resentful with no outlet, he plotted rebellion and openly denounced the crimes of Qi and his ilk.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang felt he had raced a thousand li to rescue the throne and earned towering merit, only to be blocked by treacherous ministers and denied even one audience. Smoldering with nowhere to vent, he turned to rebellion and publicly denounced Qi and his crimes.

sentences.zh: 士議嘩沸，皆指目杞，帝始寤，貶為新州司馬。

translations.literal: Officers' opinion seethed; all pointed at Qi. The Emperor at last awakened and demoted him to secretary of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Officers' talk boiled over, every finger pointing at Qi. The Emperor finally saw clearly and demoted him to secretary of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，帝即位，以崔祐甫為相，專以道德導主意，故建中初綱紀張設，赫然有貞觀風。
