translations.literal: At the beginning when the Emperor took the throne, he made Cui Youfu chancellor, who devoted himself to guiding the sovereign's mind with moral virtue; thus in the early Jianzhong era standards were prominently established, with the clear aura of the Zhenguan reign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first ascended the throne he made Cui Youfu chancellor, who led the court by moral example. In the early Jianzhong years discipline stood tall again, with something of the Zhenguan age about it.

sentences.zh: 及杞相，乃諷帝以刑名繩天下，亂敗踵及。

translations.literal: When Qi became chancellor, he persuaded the Emperor to bind the realm with legal statutes and penal names; disorder and ruin followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi took power he urged the Emperor to rule the realm through harsh law and punishment, and chaos followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 其陰害矯譎，雖國屯主辱，猶謷然肆為之。

translations.literal: His secret injuries and cunning deceit—though the state was in distress and the sovereign humiliated—he still brazenly carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: His hidden malice and twisted schemes continued even while the dynasty staggered and the sovereign suffered humiliation.

sentences.zh: 後雖斥，然帝念之不衰。

translations.literal: Though later banished, the Emperor's regard for him did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: Even after his exile the Emperor's fondness for him did not wane.

sentences.zh: 及興元赦令，俄徙吉州長史。

translations.literal: When the Xingyuan amnesty was issued, he was soon transferred to chief administrator of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xingyuan amnesty he was soon moved to chief administrator of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 杞乃曰：「上必復用我。」

translations.literal: Qi then said: 'His Majesty is sure to employ me again.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "The Emperor is bound to bring me back.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，詔拜饒州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, an edict appointed him prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan an edict made him prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中袁高當行詔書，不肯草，白宰相曰：「杞反易天常，使萬乘播遷，幸赦不誅，又委大州，失天下望。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao was to draft the edict and refused; he told the chancellors: 'Qi violated Heaven's order and drove the Emperor's carriage to wander in exile; spared by the amnesty from execution, he is now entrusted with a great prefecture—the realm's hopes are betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao, who was to draft the appointment edict, refused. He told the chancellors, "Qi overturned Heaven's order and drove the Son of Heaven into exile. Spared execution by the amnesty, he is now given a great prefecture—the empire's trust is betrayed.

sentences.zh: 宰相不悅，乃召它舍人作制，高固執不得下。

translations.literal: The chancellors were displeased and summoned another drafter to compose the decree; Gao firmly held out and it could not be issued.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors were displeased and called another drafter to write the decree, but Gao held firm and the appointment could not go forward.

sentences.zh: 於是諫臣趙需、裴佶、宇文炫、盧景亮、張薦等眾對，極言杞罪四海共棄，今復用之，忠臣寒膺，良士痛骨，必且階禍。

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrance officials Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others presented en masse, saying in the strongest terms that Qi's crimes made him rejected by all within the four seas; to employ him again would chill loyal ministers' breasts and pierce worthy gentlemen to the bone—disaster would surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others then appeared together, declaring that Qi's crimes had made him an outcast throughout the realm, that reappointing him would freeze loyal hearts and wound good men to the marrow, and that calamity would surely follow.

sentences.zh: 其言懇到。

translations.literal: Their words were earnest and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Their remonstrance was impassioned and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 帝語宰相曰：「授杞小州可乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the chancellors: 'Would appointing Qi to a small prefecture be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the chancellors, "Would it do to give Qi only a small prefecture?

sentences.zh: 李勉曰：「陛下與大州亦無難，如四方之謗何？」

translations.literal: Li Mian said: 'Your Majesty would have no difficulty even giving him a large prefecture—but what of the slander from all quarters?'
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian replied, "Your Majesty could as easily give him a large prefecture—but what of the outcry from every quarter?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔為澧州別駕。

translations.literal: An edict then made him vice-prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed him vice-prefect of Lizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 後散騎常侍李泌見，帝曰：「高等論杞事，朕可之矣！」

translations.literal: Later Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Bi was received in audience; the Emperor said: 'Regarding Gao and the others' discussion of Qi—I have accepted it!
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Bi was received in audience, the Emperor said, "On Gao and the others' remonstrance about Qi—I have accepted it!

sentences.zh: 泌頓首賀曰：「比日外謂陛下漢之桓、靈，今乃知堯、舜主也。」

translations.literal: Bi kowtowed in congratulation and said: 'These days outsiders call Your Majesty the Huan and Ling of Han; now I know you are a sovereign of Yao and Shun.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi kowtowed in congratulation. "Lately outsiders compare Your Majesty to the Han emperors Huan and Ling," he said. "Now I see you are a ruler in the mold of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 帝喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 杞遂死澧州。

translations.literal: Qi then died in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi died soon afterward in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，尚父郭子儀病甚，百官造省，不屏姬侍。

translations.literal: Initially, when Grand Mentor Guo Ziyi was gravely ill, officials of all ranks called to inquire; he did not dismiss his concubines and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Mentor Guo Ziyi fell gravely ill, officials of every rank came to inquire after him, and he did not send away his concubines and attendants.

sentences.zh: 及杞至，則屏之，隱几而待。

translations.literal: When Qi arrived, he dismissed them, leaned on his armrest, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi arrived, Ziyi dismissed them, leaned on his armrest, and waited.

sentences.zh: 家人怪問其故，子儀曰：「彼外陋內險，左右見必笑，使後得權，吾族無類矣！」

translations.literal: His household wondered and asked why; Ziyi said: 'That man is ugly outside but treacherous within—if those beside me see him they will surely laugh; should he later gain power, my clan will not survive!
translations.idiomatic: His family marveled and asked why. Ziyi said, "That man is homely outside and dangerous within. If those around me see him they will laugh—and if he ever gains power, my house will be wiped out!

sentences.zh: 崔胤崔胤，字垂休，宰相慎由子也。

translations.literal: Cui Yin—Cui Yin, courtesy name Chuixiu, was the son of Chancellor Shenyou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin—courtesy name Chuixiu—was the son of Chancellor Shenyou.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，累遷中書舍人、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, and through successive promotions became Secretariat Drafter and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through the ranks to Secretariat Drafter and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 喜陰計，附離權強，其外自處若簡重，而中險譎可畏。

translations.literal: He delighted in covert schemes, attaching himself to the powerful; outwardly he carried himself as simple and weighty, but inwardly he was perilously treacherous and to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: He loved secret plots and clung to the powerful. Outwardly he seemed plain and dignified; inwardly he was treacherous and frightening.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯屢薦之，由戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei repeatedly recommended him, and he rose from Vice Minister of Revenue to Co-signer with equal rank as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei repeatedly recommended him, and he advanced from Vice Minister of Revenue to Co-signer with equal rank as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 方王珙兄弟爭河中，以胤為節度使，不得赴，半歲，復以中書侍郎留輔政。

translations.literal: Just when the Wang Gong brothers were contending for Hezhong, Yin was made military commissioner but could not go; half a year later he returned as Vice Director of the Secretariat to remain in government.
translations.idiomatic: While the Wang Gong brothers were fighting over Hezhong, Yin was named military commissioner but could not take up the post. Half a year later he returned as Vice Director of the Secretariat and stayed at court.

sentences.zh: 及昭緯以罪誅，罷為武安節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhaowei was executed for crimes, Yin was dismissed as Military Commissioner of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaowei was executed for his crimes, Yin was removed and sent out as Military Commissioner of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 陸扆當國，時王室不競，南、北司各樹黨結藩鎮，內相淩脅。

translations.literal: When Lu Yi held the government, the royal house was not competitive; the southern and northern bureaus each formed factions and allied with military governors, and inner officials bullied and coerced one another.
translations.idiomatic: While Lu Yi directed the government the throne was weak. The southern and northern palace offices each built factions and tied themselves to military governors, and inner officials bullied one another.

sentences.zh: 胤素厚朱全忠，委心結之。

translations.literal: Yin had long been close to Zhu Quanzhong and devoted himself to forging ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had long been close to Zhu Quanzhong and threw himself into cultivating that bond.

sentences.zh: 全忠為言胤有功，不宜處外，故還相而逐扆。

translations.literal: Quanzhong spoke on Yin's behalf, saying he had merit and should not be kept outside the capital; thus Yin returned to the chancellorship and Lu Yi was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong argued that Yin had merit and should not be kept in the provinces, so Yin returned to the chancellorship and Lu Yi was pushed out.

sentences.zh: 光化初，昭宗至自華，務安反側，而胤陰為全忠地，俾擅兵四討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guanghua era, Zhaozong returned from Hua and worked to pacify the restive; yet Yin secretly made room for Quanzhong, enabling him to wield armies in all four directions on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guanghua era Zhaozong returned from Hua and tried to calm the restless factions, but Yin quietly cleared space for Quanzhong to march armies in every direction.

sentences.zh: 帝醜其行，罷為吏部尚書，復倚扆以相。

translations.literal: The Emperor loathed his conduct and dismissed him as Minister of Personnel, again relying on Lu Yi as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor detested his behavior, demoted him to Minister of Personnel, and again relied on Lu Yi as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 會清海無帥，因拜胤清海節度使。

translations.literal: As it happened Qinghai had no commander, so Yin was appointed Military Commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghai happened to lack a commander, Yin was appointed its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 始，昭緯死，皆王摶等白髮其奸，胤坐是賜罷，內銜憾。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Zhaowei died, Wang Tuan and others had disclosed his treachery; Yin was consequently dismissed and harbored resentment within.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhaowei died, Wang Tuan and others had exposed Yin's treachery, and Yin was dismissed—nursing a grudge ever since.

sentences.zh: 既與摶同宰相，胤議悉去中官，摶不助，請徐圖之。

translations.literal: Once he served as chancellor alongside Tuan, Yin proposed removing all palace eunuchs; Tuan would not assist and asked to proceed gradually.
translations.idiomatic: When he later served as chancellor with Tuan, Yin proposed purging all palace eunuchs. Tuan would not help and urged a slower approach.

sentences.zh: 及是不欲外除，即漏其語於全忠，令露劾摶交敕使共危國，罪當誅。

translations.literal: Not wishing to be sent outside the capital on this occasion, he leaked Tuan's words to Quanzhong and had him openly impeach Tuan for colluding with decree-bearers to endanger the state—the crime merited execution.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to accept exile, he leaked Tuan's words to Quanzhong and had him publicly accuse Tuan of colluding with decree-bearing eunuchs to endanger the state—a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 胤次湖南，召還守司空、門下侍郎、平章事，兼領度支、鹽鐵、戶部使，而賜摶死，並誅中尉宋道弼、景務修，繇是權震天下，雖宦官亦累息。

translations.literal: Yin was stopped at Hunan, then recalled to serve as Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Counselor, concurrently heading the Revenue Bureau and the Salt and Iron and Revenue commissions; Tuan was condemned to death, and Palace Directors Song Daobu and Jing Wuxiu were also executed. From this his power shook the realm—even the eunuchs repeatedly quailed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was halted in Hunan, then recalled as Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Counselor, while also heading the Revenue Bureau and the Salt and Iron and Revenue commissions. Tuan was condemned to death, and Palace Directors Song Daobu and Jing Wuxiu were executed with him. From then on Yin's power shook the realm—even the eunuchs kept their heads down.

sentences.zh: 至是，四拜宰相，世謂「崔四入」。

translations.literal: By this point he had entered the chancellorship four times; the age called him 'Cui's Four Entries.'
translations.idiomatic: By then he had become chancellor four times, and people called him "Cui the Four-Time Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 劉季述幽帝東內，奉德王監國，畏全忠強，雖深怨胤，不敢殺，止罷政事。

translations.literal: Liu Jishu imprisoned the Emperor in the Eastern Inner Palace and installed Prince De as regent; fearing Quanzhong's strength, though he deeply hated Yin he dared not kill him and only stripped him of government duties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jishu confined the Emperor in the Eastern Inner Palace and set Prince De to govern as regent. Fearing Quanzhong's power, he hated Yin deeply yet dared not kill him, and only removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 胤趣全忠以師西，問所以幽帝狀。

translations.literal: Yin urged Quanzhong to march west with his army and asked how the Emperor had been imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pressed Quanzhong to march west and asked for the full story of the Emperor's confinement.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃使張存敬攻河中，掠晉、絳。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Hezhong and raid Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Hezhong and ravage Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 神策軍大將孫德昭常忿閹尹廢辱天子，胤令判官石戩與遊，乘間伺察。

translations.literal: Sun Dezhao, a general of the Divine Strategy Army, often seethed that the eunuch lords had deposed and humiliated the Son of Heaven; Yin had his aide Shi Jian associate with him and watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dezhao, a general of the Divine Strategy Army, often burned with rage that eunuch lords had deposed and shamed the Son of Heaven. Yin had his aide Shi Jian cultivate his company and watch for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 德昭飲酣必泣，胤揣得其情，乃使戩說曰：「自季述廢天子，天下之人未嘗忘，武夫義臣搏手憤惋。

translations.literal: When Dezhao drank deeply he always wept; Yin divined his sentiment and had Shi persuade him, saying: 'Since Jishu deposed the Son of Heaven, the people of the realm have never forgotten; martial men and loyal ministers wring their hands in rage and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao wept whenever he drank deeply. Yin read his heart and sent Shi to say, "Since Jishu deposed the Son of Heaven, the realm has never forgotten. Martial men and loyal ministers clench their fists in fury.

sentences.zh: 今謀反者特季述、仲先耳，它人劫於威，無與也。

translations.literal: Today those who plotted rebellion are only Jishu and Zhongxian; the others are coerced by fear and had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jishu and Zhongxian truly plotted this. The rest were bullied into compliance and had no share in the crime.

sentences.zh: 君能乘此誅二豎，復天子，取功名乎？

translations.literal: Sir, can you seize this moment to execute the two vermin, restore the Son of Heaven, and win fame and merit?
translations.idiomatic: Can you seize this moment, kill those two vermin, restore the Son of Heaven, and win glory for yourself?

sentences.zh: 即不早計，將有無之者。」

translations.literal: If you do not plan early, others will do it for you.
translations.idiomatic: If you wait too long, someone else will beat you to it.

sentences.zh: 德昭感寤，乃告以胤謀。

translations.literal: Dezhao was moved to understanding and was told of Yin's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Dezhao was let in on Yin's plan.

sentences.zh: 德昭許諾，胤斬帶為誓。

translations.literal: Dezhao pledged agreement; Yin cut his belt as a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao agreed, and Yin cut his belt as a pledge.

sentences.zh: 俄而季述、仲先誅，以功進司徒，不就，復輔政，並還使領。

translations.literal: Soon Jishu and Zhongxian were executed; for his merit he was promoted to Minister of Education but declined; he returned to assist in government and recovered his commissionerships as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jishu and Zhongxian were killed. For his service Dezhao was offered Minister of Education but declined; he returned to assist in government and regained his commissionerships as well.

sentences.zh: 帝德之，延見或不名，以字呼之，寵遇無比。

translations.literal: The Emperor was grateful to him; when receiving him in audience he sometimes omitted his name and called him by his courtesy name— favor unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply grateful. In audience he sometimes omitted Yin's name and called him by his courtesy name—a favor without parallel.

sentences.zh: 天復元年，全忠已取河中，進逼同、華。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Quanzhong had already taken Hezhong and pressed forward against Tong and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianfu, Quanzhong had already seized Hezhong and was pressing Tong and Hua.

sentences.zh: 中尉韓全誨以胤與全忠善，恐導之翦除君側，乃白罷政事，未及免，倉卒挾帝幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Palace Director Han Quanhui, because Yin was on good terms with Quanzhong, feared he would guide him to prune those beside the sovereign; he petitioned to strip Yin of government duties, but before the dismissal took effect he hastily escorted the Emperor to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Director Han Quanhui, seeing Yin's closeness to Quanzhong, feared Yin would lead him to purge the court. He petitioned to remove Yin from office, but before the order could take effect he hurried the Emperor off to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 胤怨帝見廢，不肯從，召全忠以兵迎天子，令太子太師盧渥率群臣迎全忠。

translations.literal: Yin resented that the Emperor had been deposed and refused to follow; he summoned Quanzhong with troops to welcome the Son of Heaven and ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Lu Wo to lead the officials to receive Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin resented the Emperor's forced removal and refused to go along. He called Quanzhong to march with his army and welcome the Son of Heaven, and ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Lu Wo to lead the officials out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 始，全忠至華，遣幕府裴鑄奏事。

translations.literal: At first, when Quanzhong reached Hua, he sent his staff member Pei Zhu to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong first reached Hua, he sent his staff member Pei Zhu to report to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，聽來朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no choice but to allow him to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had no choice but to permit him to come to audience.

sentences.zh: 至是胤為之謀，乃以兵迫行在。

translations.literal: At this point Yin plotted on his behalf, and thus used troops to press upon the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yin had devised the plan and sent troops to pressure the emperor's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔趣還鎮，因詔遣渥等俱西。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict urging return to his garrison, and by edict ordered Wo and the others to go west together.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict ordering him back to his command, and also ordered Lu Wo and the others to proceed west together.

sentences.zh: 全忠上表具言：「向書詔皆出宰相，乃今知非陛下意，為所詿誤。

translations.literal: Quanzhong submitted a memorial in full detail: "The edicts received earlier all came from the chancellors; only now do I know they were not Your Majesty's intent and that I was led astray by them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong submitted a detailed memorial: "The edicts I received all came from the chancellors. I now realize they did not reflect Your Majesty's intent—I was misled.

sentences.zh: 師業入關，請得與李茂貞約釋憾以迎乘輿。」

translations.literal: Shiye entered the pass and requested permission to make a pact with Li Maozhen to release old grievances and welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shiye entered the pass and asked to arrange with Li Maozhen a reconciliation so they could welcome the emperor back.

sentences.zh: 茂貞劾奏：「胤畜死士，用度支使榷利，令親信陳班與京兆府募兵保所居坊。

translations.literal: Maozhen impeached and memorialized: "Yin keeps death-defying warriors, uses the commissioner of revenue to monopolize profits, and ordered his trusted follower Chen Ban and the Capital Prefecture to recruit soldiers to guard the ward where he lives.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen memorialized against him: "Yin keeps assassins, uses the revenue commissioner to squeeze monopoly profits, and has his confidant Chen Ban and the capital prefecture recruit troops to guard his ward.

sentences.zh: 天子出次，遣使者五輩往召，安臥不動，一奉表陳謝。」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven went out to his temporary lodging, he sent five rounds of envoys to summon him; he lay at ease unmoved, submitting only one memorial of apology."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to a temporary lodging, five envoys were sent to summon Yin, but he lay unmoved and merely submitted one apologetic memorial."

sentences.zh: 時帝見全忠表，亦大恚，因下詔顯責之，以工部尚書罷知政事，胤出居華州。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor saw Quanzhong's memorial and also grew greatly angry; he therefore issued an edict openly rebuking Yin, removed him from handling governmental affairs with the post of Minister of Works, and Yin went out to reside at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read Quanzhong's memorial he was furious. He issued an edict openly censuring Yin, stripped him of the chancellorship while retaining him as Minister of Works, and Yin withdrew to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，天復後宦官尤屈事胤，事無不咨。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after Tianfu the eunuchs especially submitted to serving Yin; on matters none went unconsulted.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianfu the eunuchs were especially deferential to Yin and consulted him on everything.

sentences.zh: 每議政禁中，至繼以燭，請盡誅中官，以宮人掌內司事。

translations.literal: Whenever they discussed governance within the forbidden quarters, it went on until candles were joined one after another; he requested executing all palace officials and having palace women manage inner bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Their policy debates in the palace often ran late into the night, candle after candle. Yin proposed executing all eunuchs and putting palace women in charge of inner court business.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨等密知之，共於帝前求哀。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and the others secretly learned of it and together begged for mercy before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanhui and others learned of this in secret and together pleaded for their lives before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃詔胤後當密封，無口陳。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that hereafter Yin must submit sealed memorials and make no oral statements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered that Yin must submit sealed memorials in future and not speak his proposals aloud.

sentences.zh: 中官益恐，滋欲得其謀，乃求知書美人宗柔等內左右以刺陰事。

translations.literal: The palace officials grew all the more fearful and increasingly wished to learn his plans; they therefore sought out literate palace beauties Zong Rou and others as inner attendants to spy on secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs grew more terrified and were desperate to learn his plans, so they recruited literate palace women like Zong Rou as inner attendants to uncover his secrets.

sentences.zh: 胤計稍露，宦者或相泣無憀，不自安，劫幸之謀固矣。

translations.literal: Yin's plans were slightly exposed; the eunuchs sometimes wept together in idleness and unease; the plot to seize the emperor was firm.
translations.idiomatic: As Yin's plot leaked, some eunuchs wept together in despair. Uneasy, they settled firmly on a plan to abduct the emperor.

sentences.zh: 居華時，為全忠數畫醜計。

translations.literal: While residing at Hua, he several times devised sinister plans for Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: While at Hua, he repeatedly plotted wicked schemes for Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠引兵還屯河中，胤迎謁渭橋，奉觴為全忠壽，自歌以釂酒。

translations.literal: Quanzhong led his troops back to encamp at Hezhong; Yin went out to greet and pay respects at Weiqiao Bridge, raised a cup to toast Quanzhong's longevity, and sang himself to drain the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong withdrew his army to garrison Hezhong. Yin met him at Weiqiao Bridge, offered a cup to wish him long life, and sang a song to drain the toast.

sentences.zh: 會茂貞殺全誨等，與全忠約和。

translations.literal: It happened that Maozhen killed Quanhui and the others and made a pact of peace with Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Then Maozhen killed Quanhui and the others and made peace with Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 帝急召之，墨詔者四、朱劄三，皆辭疾。

translations.literal: The Emperor urgently summoned him—four times with ink edicts and three with vermilion notes—all declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently summoned him—four ink edicts and three vermilion notes—and each time Yin pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 及帝出鳳翔，幸全忠軍，乃迎謁於道，復拜平章事，進位司徒，兼判六軍諸衛事，詔徙家舍右軍，賜帷帳器用十車。

translations.literal: When the Emperor left Fengxiang and visited Quanzhong's army, he then met and paid respects on the road, was again appointed Associate Chancellor, advanced to Minister of Education, and concurrently adjudicated the Six Armies and guard offices; an edict moved his household to lodge in the Right Army and bestowed ten cartloads of curtains, tents, and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left Fengxiang and went to Quanzhong's camp, Yin met him on the road. He was again made chancellor, promoted to Minister of Education, and put in charge of the Six Armies and guards. His household was ordered to lodge in the Right Army camp and he was given ten carts of furnishings.

sentences.zh: 胤遂奏：「高祖、太宗無內侍典軍，天寶後宦人浸盛，德宗分羽林衛為左右神策軍，令宦者主之，以二千人為率。

translations.literal: Yin then memorialized: "Emperors Gaozu and Taizong had no inner attendants commanding armies. After Tianbao the eunuchs gradually flourished; Emperor Dezong divided the Feathered Forest Guard into Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and had eunuchs command them, with two thousand men as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then submitted a memorial: "Gaozu and Taizong had no eunuchs commanding troops. After Tianbao eunuchs grew ever stronger; Dezong split the Feathered Forest Guard into the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and put eunuchs in charge at two thousand men each.

sentences.zh: 其後參掌機密，至內務百司悉歸中人，共相彌縫為不法，朝廷微弱，禍始於此。

translations.literal: Thereafter they jointly managed secret affairs, until all inner offices and the hundred bureaus fell to the palace insiders; they covered up one another in wrongdoing, the court grew weak, and the calamity began here.
translations.idiomatic: They soon shared in state secrets, and eventually every inner office came under eunuch control. They covered for one another's crimes, the court was enfeebled, and the disaster began here.

sentences.zh: 請罷左右神策、內諸司使、諸道監軍。」

translations.literal: He requested abolishing the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies, the commissioners of the inner bureaus, and the army supervisors in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies, the inner-bureau commissioners, and the circuit army supervisors all be abolished.

sentences.zh: 於是中外宦官悉誅，天子傳導詔命，只用宮人寵顏等。

translations.literal: Thereupon eunuchs within and without were all executed; the Son of Heaven transmitted and announced edicts using only palace women Chongyan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs inside and outside the palace were then all executed. Palace women like Chongyan alone carried the emperor's edicts.

sentences.zh: 帝之在鳳翔，以廬光啟、蘇檢為相，胤皆逐殺之，分斥從幸近臣陸扆等三十餘人，惟裴贄孤立可制，留與偕秉政。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Fengxiang, he had Lu Guangqi and Su Jian as chancellors; Yin drove them out and killed them all, dismissed more than thirty close ministers who had accompanied the imperial progress such as Lu Yi, and only Pei Zhan stood alone and could be controlled—he was kept to share governance together.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Fengxiang, Lu Guangqi and Su Jian had served as chancellors; Yin drove them out and had them killed. He expelled more than thirty courtiers who had followed the emperor, such as Lu Yi, leaving only Pei Zhan, isolated and manageable, to share power.

sentences.zh: 帝動靜一決於胤，無敢言者。

translations.literal: The Emperor's every move and stillness was decided entirely by Yin; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Every move the emperor made was decided by Yin, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 胤議以皇子為元帥，全忠副之，示褒崇其功。

translations.literal: Yin proposed making an imperial prince the commander-in-chief with Quanzhong as deputy, to show praise and elevation of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yin proposed making an imperial prince commander-in-chief with Quanzhong as his deputy—a gesture meant to honor Quanzhong's achievements.

sentences.zh: 全忠內利輝王沖幼，故胤藉以請。

translations.literal: Quanzhong inwardly favored Prince Hui for being young, so Yin used this in making the request.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong privately favored Prince Hui because he was young, and Yin framed his request accordingly.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「濮王長，若何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Prince Pu is the eldest—what of that?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Prince Pu is the eldest—what about him?

sentences.zh: 還禁中，召翰林學士韓偓以謀。

translations.literal: Returning to the forbidden quarters, he summoned Han Wo, a Hanlin academician, to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the palace he summoned Hanlin academician Han Wo for advice.

sentences.zh: 偓陰佐胤，卒不能卻。

translations.literal: Han Wo secretly aided Yin and in the end could not turn him back.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo secretly sided with Yin, and in the end could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 全忠還東，到長樂，群臣班辭，胤獨至霸橋置酒，乙夜乃還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned east; when he reached Changle, the ministers took their leave in court order, but Yin alone went to Baxia Bridge to set out wine and did not return until the second watch of the night.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong headed east. At Changle the ministers took formal leave, but Yin alone went to Baxia Bridge to host a banquet and did not return until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 帝即召問：「全忠安否？」

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately summoned him and asked: "Is Quanzhong safe and well?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him at once and asked, "Is Quanzhong safe and well?

sentences.zh: 與飲，命宮人為舞劍曲，戊夜乃出，賜二宮人，固讓乃許。

translations.literal: He drank with him, ordered palace women to perform the sword-dance song; he left only at the fifth watch, was granted two palace women, firmly declined, and only then was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They drank together. The emperor had palace women perform a sword-dance song. Yin did not leave until the fifth watch. Two palace women were granted him; he refused firmly before finally accepting.

sentences.zh: 是時天子孤危，威令盡去，胤之劫持類如此。

translations.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven was isolated and endangered, authority and commands were entirely gone—Yin's domination was mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was isolated and powerless, his authority gone. Yin's hold over him was mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 進侍中、魏國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Duke of Wei State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and made Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自鳳翔還，揣全忠將篡奪，顧己宰相，恐一日及禍，欲握兵自固，謬謂全忠曰：「京師迫茂貞，不可無備，須募軍以守。

translations.literal: Since returning from Fengxiang, sensing Quanzhong would usurp, considering himself chancellor, fearing one day disaster would reach him, he wished to grasp troops to secure himself; he falsely told Quanzhong: "The capital is pressed by Maozhen and cannot be without defenses; troops must be recruited to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Fengxiang, sensing Quanzhong's ambitions and fearing that as chancellor he might one day be ruined, Yin wanted troops of his own. He falsely told Quanzhong, "Maozhen threatens the capital—we must recruit a garrison to defend it.

sentences.zh: 今左右龍武、羽林、神策，播幸之餘，無見兵。

translations.literal: Now the Left and Right Dragon Martial, Feathered Forest, and Divine Strategy—after the imperial progress wanderings, there are no visible troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Martial, Feathered Forest, and Divine Strategy guards have been scattered since the emperor's forced wanderings—there are hardly any troops left.

sentences.zh: 請軍置四步將，將二百五十人；

translations.literal: He requested establishing four infantry commanders, each commanding two hundred fifty men;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to raise four infantry commanders of two hundred fifty men each;

sentences.zh: 一騎將，將百人。

translations.literal: and one cavalry commander commanding one hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: and one cavalry commander of one hundred men.

sentences.zh: 使番休遞侍。」

translations.literal: Have them rotate in relief and serve in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They would rotate duty in shifts.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹鄭元規為六軍諸衛副使，陳班為威遠軍使，募卒於市。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuangui, Prefect of the Capital, was made deputy commissioner of the Six Armies and guards; Chen Ban was made commander of the Weiyuan Army; soldiers were recruited in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuangui, the capital prefect, was made deputy commissioner of the Six Armies and guards; Chen Ban was made commander of the Weiyuan Army; and troops were recruited openly in the markets.

sentences.zh: 全忠知其意，陽相然許。

translations.literal: Quanzhong knew his intent and outwardly agreed and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw through him but pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 胤乃毀浮圖，取銅鐵為兵仗。

translations.literal: Yin then destroyed pagodas, taking copper and iron to make weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then demolished pagodas to melt down their bronze and iron for arms.

sentences.zh: 全忠陰令汴人數百應募，以其子友倫入宿衛。

translations.literal: Quanzhong secretly ordered several hundred men of Bian to enlist, and had his son Youlun enter palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong secretly had several hundred men from Bian enlist, and sent his son Youlun into palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 會為球戲，墜馬死，全忠疑胤陰計，大怒。

translations.literal: It happened that during ball-play he fell from a horse and died; Quanzhong suspected Yin's hidden plot and grew greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: During a ball game Youlun fell from his horse and died. Quanzhong suspected Yin had plotted it and was furious.

sentences.zh: 時傳胤將挾帝幸荊、襄，而全忠方謀脅乘輿都洛，懼其異議，密表胤專權亂國，請誅之。

translations.literal: At the time it was rumored Yin would seize the Emperor and go to Jing and Xiang, while Quanzhong was just then plotting to coerce the imperial carriage to make the capital at Luoyang; fearing dissent, he secretly memorialized that Yin monopolized power and threw the state into disorder, requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Yin meant to take the emperor to Jing and Xiang, while Quanzhong was planning to force the court to move the capital to Luoyang. Fearing opposition, he secretly memorialized that Yin's monopoly on power was ruining the state and asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 即罷為太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was immediately dismissed to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was immediately demoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 全忠令其子友諒以兵圍開化坊第，殺胤，汴士皆突出，市人爭投瓦礫擊其屍，年五十一，元規、陳班等皆死，實天復四年正月。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered his son Youliang to surround Yin's residence in Kaihua Ward with troops and kill Yin; the Bian soldiers all burst out; market people vied to throw tiles and stones at his corpse. He was fifty-one. Yuangui, Chen Ban, and others all died—the actual date was the first month of the fourth year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent his son Youliang with troops to surround Yin's mansion in Kaihua Ward and kill him. The Bian soldiers burst out; townspeople hurled tiles and stones at his corpse. Yin was fifty-one. Yuangui, Chen Ban, and others were killed too. This was the first month of Tianfu year four.

sentences.zh: 胤罷凡三日死，死十日，全忠脅帝遷洛，發長安居人悉東，徹屋木自渭循河下。

translations.literal: Three days after Yin's dismissal he died; ten days after his death Quanzhong coerced the Emperor to move the capital to Luoyang, dispatching all Chang'an residents east, tearing down houses and sending timber down from the Wei River along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yin died just three days after his dismissal. Ten days later Quanzhong forced the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang, sending every Chang'an resident east and dismantling buildings to float the timber down the Wei and along the river.

sentences.zh: 老幼系路，啼號不絕，皆大罵曰：「國賊崔胤導全忠賣社稷，使我及此！」

translations.literal: Old and young lined the roads, weeping and wailing without cease; all cursed loudly: "The traitor to the state Cui Yin led Quanzhong to sell the altars of soil and grain, bringing us to this!
translations.idiomatic: Old and young lined the roads, wailing without end. They cursed loudly, "That traitor Cui Yin guided Quanzhong to sell out the realm and bring us to this!

sentences.zh: 先是，全忠雖據河南，顧強諸侯相持，未敢決移國。

translations.literal: Earlier, although Quanzhong held Henan, considering the powerful feudatories locked in mutual standoff, he did not dare decide to shift the state.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, though Quanzhong held Henan, the strong regional lords kept one another in check and he dared not move to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 及胤間內隙，與相結，得梯其禍，取朝權以成強大，終亡天下，胤身屠宗滅。

translations.literal: When Yin created internal rifts and allied with him, Quanzhong was able to climb by his calamity, take court power to grow strong, and in the end lost the realm; Yin himself was slaughtered and his clan destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin exploited court divisions and allied with Quanzhong, letting him ride one crisis after another to seize court power and grow mighty—until the Tang was destroyed and Yin himself was slaughtered along with his clan.

sentences.zh: 世言慎由晚無子，遇異浮屠，以術求，乃生胤，字緇郎。

translations.literal: The world says Shenyou in his later years had no son; he met a strange Buddhist monk and by arts sought one, and thus bore Yin, courtesy name Zilang.
translations.idiomatic: People said Shenyou had no son in his later years. He met an eccentric monk and used occult arts to obtain an heir—thus Yin was born, with the courtesy name Zilang.

sentences.zh: 及為相，其季父安潛唶曰：「吾父兄刻苦以持門戶，終為緇郎壞之！」

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, his uncle Anqian clicked his tongue and said: "Our fathers and elder brothers toiled bitterly to maintain the family gate, yet in the end Zilang ruined it!
translations.idiomatic: When Yin became chancellor, his uncle Anqian lamented, "Our fathers and elder brothers toiled to uphold this house, and Zilang ruined it in the end!

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯崔昭緯字蘊曜，其先清河人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei—Cui Zhaowei, courtesy name Yunyao; his ancestors were men of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei, courtesy name Yunyao, came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 至昭宗時仕浸顯，以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事，居位凡八年，累進尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhaozong's time his service gradually grew prominent; as Vice Minister of Revenue he was made Associate Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery; he held office altogether eight years and was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose steadily. As Vice Minister of Revenue he became associate chancellor, served eight years in all, and was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 性險刻，密結中人，外連強諸侯，內制天子以固其權。

translations.literal: His nature was sinister and harsh; he secretly allied with palace insiders, outwardly linked with powerful feudatories, and inwardly controlled the Son of Heaven to secure his power.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous and harsh by nature, he secretly allied with eunuchs and powerful warlords abroad while controlling the emperor at court to cement his power.

sentences.zh: 令族人鋋事王行瑜邠寧幕府。

translations.literal: He had his clansman Chan serve in Wang Xingyu's Binning military commission staff.
translations.idiomatic: He placed his kinsman Chan on the staff of Wang Xingyu's Binning command.

sentences.zh: 每它宰相建議，或詔令有不便於己，必使鋋密告行瑜，使上書訾訐，己則陰阿助之。

translations.literal: Whenever other chancellors made proposals, or edicts and orders were inconvenient to himself, he always had Chan secretly inform Xingyu, have him submit memorials denouncing and impeaching, while he himself secretly sided with and aided them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever another chancellor proposed something, or an edict went against his interests, he had Chan secretly tell Xingyu to submit attacking memorials while he quietly backed them from behind.

sentences.zh: 方是時，帝室微，人主若贅斿然。

translations.literal: Just then the imperial house was weak; the ruler was like a superfluous streamer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the throne was enfeebled; the emperor was little more than a figurehead.

sentences.zh: 始，帝委杜讓能調兵食以討鳳翔，昭緯方倚李茂貞、行瑜為重，陰得其計，則走告之，激使稱兵向闕，遂殺讓能。

translations.literal: At the start the Emperor entrusted Du Rangneng to marshal troops and provisions to attack Fengxiang; Zhaowei was then relying on Li Maozhen and Xingyu as his weight; when he secretly learned their plan he would run and inform them, inciting them to raise troops toward the capital, and thus Rangneng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor put Du Rangneng in charge of supplies for the campaign against Fengxiang, Zhaowei, who leaned on Li Maozhen and Xingyu, learned the plans in secret and raced to warn them, goading them to march on the capital—Rangneng was then killed.

sentences.zh: 後又導三鎮兵殺韋昭度等。

translations.literal: Later he also guided the three-garrison armies to kill Wei Zhaodu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He later guided the armies of the Three Circuits to kill Wei Zhaodu and others.

sentences.zh: 帝性剛明，不堪忍，會誅行瑜，乃罷昭緯為右仆射。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was firm and clear-sighted; he could not endure it. When Xingyu was executed, Zhaowei was then dismissed to Right Vice Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was resolute and clear-sighted and would not tolerate it. When Xingyu was executed, Zhaowei was demoted to Right Vice Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 復請朱全忠薦己，又厚賂諸王，為所奏，貶梧州司馬，下詔條其五罪，賜死。

translations.literal: He again asked Zhu Quanzhong to recommend him; he also lavishly bribed the princes, was reported by them, was demoted to military adjutant of Wuzhou, an edict enumerated his five crimes, and death was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked Zhu Quanzhong to recommend him and heavily bribed the princes, but they reported him. He was demoted to Wuzhou adjutant; an edict listed five crimes and ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 行次江陵，使者至，斬之。

translations.literal: En route at Jiangling, the envoy arrived and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jiangling, the executioner's envoy arrived and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 鋋亦誅。

translations.literal: Chan was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chan was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 柳璨柳璨字炤之，公綽族孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Can—Liu Can, courtesy name Zhaozhi, a clansman grandson of Gongchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, courtesy name Zhaozhi, was a descendant of Liu Gongchuo's clan line.

sentences.zh: 為人鄙野，其家不以諸柳齒。

translations.literal: As a person he was crude and rustic; his family did not rank him with the various Liu clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Crude and rustic in manner, his own family did not count him among the Liu kin.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，好學，晝采薪給費，夜然葉照書，強記，多所通涉。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, fond of learning; by day he gathered firewood for expenses, by night he burned leaves to illuminate books; he had strong memory and broadly mastered many subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he loved learning. By day he gathered firewood for money; by night he burned leaves to read by. He had a prodigious memory and read widely.

sentences.zh: 譏訶劉子玄《史通》，著《析微》，時或稱之。

translations.literal: He ridiculed Liu Zixuan's Shitong and authored Xiwai; at times people praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Liu Zixuan's Shitong and wrote Xiwai, which won some praise.

sentences.zh: 顏蕘判史館，引為直學士，由是益知名。

translations.literal: Yan Rao was in charge of the History Office and brought him in as a direct academician; from this he grew even more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rao, head of the History Office, made him a direct academician, and his reputation grew.

sentences.zh: 遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 昭宗好文，待李磎最厚，磎死，內常求似磎者。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong loved literature and treated Li Xi most generously; when Xi died, within the palace they constantly sought one like Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong loved letters and favored Li Xi above all. After Xi died the court sought someone like him.

sentences.zh: 或薦璨才高，試文，帝稱善，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Can for high talent; his writing was tested; the Emperor praised it and promoted him to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended Can's brilliance. His writing was tested; the emperor approved and made him a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 崔胤死，昭宗密許璨宰相，外無知者。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin died, Emperor Zhaozong secretly promised Can the chancellorship; outside none knew.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Yin died, Emperor Zhaozong secretly promised Can the chancellorship; no one outside knew.

sentences.zh: 日暮自禁中出，騶士傳呼宰相，人皆大驚。

translations.literal: At dusk he came out from the forbidden quarters; escort riders announced "Chancellor!"—all were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he left the palace; mounted escorts called out "Chancellor!"—everyone was stunned.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝謂學士承旨張文蔚曰：「璨材可用，今擢為相，應授何官？」

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor said to Academic Administrator Zhang Wenwei: "Can's talent can be used; now that I am promoting him to chancellor, what office should be granted?
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to chief academician Zhang Wenwei, "Can's talent is usable. I am making him chancellor—what title should he receive?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「用賢不計資。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In employing the worthy one does not calculate seniority."
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei replied, "When appointing the worthy, rank should not matter."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諫議大夫可乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Would Remonstrating and Advising Grandee do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Would Remonstrating Advisor suffice?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「唯唯。」

translations.literal: He said: "Yes, yes."
translations.idiomatic: Yes, yes," he answered.

sentences.zh: 遂以諫議大夫同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Thereupon as Remonstrating and Advising Grandee he was made Associate Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Can was then made associate chancellor with the title Remonstrating Advisor.

sentences.zh: 起布衣，至是不四歲，其暴貴近世所未有。

translations.literal: Rising from common cloth, until then not four years—such sudden ennoblement had no parallel in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: From commoner to chancellor in under four years—such a sudden rise was unheard of in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 裴樞、獨孤損、崔遠皆宿望舊臣，與同位，頗輕之，璨內以為怨。

translations.literal: Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and Cui Yuan were all longstanding esteemed old ministers; sharing the same rank they rather looked down on him, and Can inwardly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and Cui Yuan were senior ministers of long standing. Sharing rank with Can, they looked down on him, and he nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠圖篡殺，宿衛士皆汴人，璨一厚結之，與蔣玄暉、張廷範尤相得。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong plotted usurpation and killing; the palace guard soldiers were all men of Bian; Can on the whole bonded closely with them, and was especially intimate with Jiang Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was plotting regicide. The palace guards were all from Bian, and Can closely cultivated them, getting on especially well with Jiang Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan.

sentences.zh: 既挾全忠，故朝權皆歸之。

translations.literal: Having relied on Quanzhong, court power all fell to him.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by Quanzhong, court power passed entirely to Can.

sentences.zh: 進中書侍郎、判戶部，封河東縣男。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue; enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and put in charge of the Ministry of Revenue, and enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，長星出太微、文昌間，占者曰：「君臣皆不利，宜多殺以塞天變。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou, a long comet appeared between Supreme Palace and Literary Glory; diviners said: "Ruler and ministers are both unfavored—one should kill many to block the heaven-sent change.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year two a comet appeared between the Supreme Palace and Literary Glory constellations. Diviners said, "This bodes ill for emperor and ministers alike—many must be killed to appease heaven.

sentences.zh: 玄暉、廷範乃與璨謀殺大臣宿有望者。

translations.literal: Xuanhui and Tingfan then with Can plotted to kill great ministers of longstanding esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui and Tingfan then plotted with Can to kill senior ministers of standing.

sentences.zh: 璨手疏所仇冒若獨孤損等三十餘人，皆誅死，天下以為冤。

translations.literal: Can in his own hand listed those he hated and bore grudges against, such as Dugu Sun and more than thirty others; all were executed; the realm considered it wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: Can personally listed more than thirty men he hated, including Dugu Sun. All were executed, and the realm regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞之，不善也。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard of it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong heard of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 其後急於九錫，宣徽北院使王殷者構璨等，言其有貳，故禮不至。

translations.literal: Thereafter eager for the nine bestowals, Wang Yin, commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat, framed Can and the others, saying they had divided loyalties, hence the rites did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong grew impatient for the nine bestowals, Wang Yin of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat framed Can and his allies, claiming disloyalty—that was why the rites had not been performed.

sentences.zh: 玄暉懼，自往辨解。

translations.literal: Xuanhui was afraid and went himself to explain and clear the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xuanhui went in person to explain.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒罵曰：「爾與柳璨輩沮我，不由九錫，作天子不得邪？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong angrily cursed: "You and Liu Can's lot are obstructing me—without going through the nine bestowals, can't I become Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong raged: "You and Liu Can's crowd are blocking me—must I have the nine bestowals before I can become emperor?

sentences.zh: 璨懼，即脅哀帝曰：「人望歸元帥矣，陛下宜揖讓以授終。」

translations.literal: Can was afraid and immediately coerced Emperor Ai: "Popular expectation returns to the Marshal—Your Majesty should yield by bowing and surrender to conclude."
translations.idiomatic: Can, terrified, immediately pressured Emperor Ai: "The people's hopes are with the Marshal. Your Majesty should abdicate in favor of him."

sentences.zh: 璨請自行，進拜司空，為冊禮使，即日進道。

translations.literal: Can requested to go himself, was promoted and invested as Minister of Works, made commissioner of enthronement rites, and that same day advanced on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Can volunteered to carry the message. He was promoted to Minister of Works and made commissioner of enthronement rites, setting out that same day.

sentences.zh: 及玄暉死，而全忠恚璨背己，貶登州刺史，俄除名為民，流崖州，尋斬之。

translations.literal: When Xuanhui died and Quanzhong resented Can for turning against him, Can was demoted to Prefect of Deng Prefecture; soon his name was removed and he was made a commoner, exiled to Yazhou, and soon beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanhui died, Quanzhong, angry that Can had betrayed him, demoted Can to prefect of Dengzhou, then stripped his rank, exiled him to Yazhou, and soon had him executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑悔咤曰：「負國賊柳璨，死宜矣！」

translations.literal: Facing execution he regretted and cried: "The traitor to the state Liu Can—death is fitting!
translations.idiomatic: At the execution block he cried in remorse, "The traitor Liu Can deserves to die!

sentences.zh: 弟瑀、瑊皆榜死。

translations.literal: His brothers Yu and Jian were both beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Yu and Jian were both flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 玄暉者，少賤，不得其系著。

translations.literal: As for Xuanhui, in youth he was lowly; his lineage could not be traced and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui came from humble beginnings; his lineage was unknown.

sentences.zh: 事朱全忠為腹心。

translations.literal: He served Zhu Quanzhong as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhu Quanzhong as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷，玄暉為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved east, Xuanhui became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was moved east, Jiang Xuanhui was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝駐陜州，術家言星緯不常，且有大變，宜須冬幸洛。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Shan Prefecture. Astrologers said the stars were irregular and a great calamity was imminent; he ought to travel to Luoyang in winter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped at Shan Prefecture. Astrologers warned that the stars were out of order and a great upheaval was coming; the court should wait until winter before proceeding to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝度全忠必篡，命衛官高瑰持帛詔賜王建，告以脅遷，且言：「全忠以兵二萬治洛陽，將盡去我左右，君宜與茂貞、克用、行密同盟，傳檄襄、魏、幽、鎮，使各以軍迎我還京師。」

translations.literal: The emperor judged that Quanzhong would surely usurp the throne. He ordered the guard officer Gao Gui to carry an edict written on silk and bestow it on Wang Jian, informing him of the forced relocation, and saying: "Quanzhong is rebuilding Luoyang with twenty thousand troops and will remove all those around me. You should ally with Maozhen, Keyong, and Xingmi, issue proclamations to Xiang, Wei, You, and Zhen, and have each region send troops to welcome me back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sure Quanzhong meant to seize the throne. He ordered the guard officer Gao Gui to carry a silk edict to Wang Jian, telling him of the forced move and saying, "Quanzhong is rebuilding Luoyang with twenty thousand men and will strip away everyone at my side. You should join Maozhen, Keyong, and Xingmi in alliance, send proclamations to Xiang, Wei, You, and Zhen, and have each of them march to bring me home to the capital."

sentences.zh: 又詔全忠：「後方娠，須十月乃東。」

translations.literal: He also sent an edict to Quanzhong: "The empress is pregnant; I cannot travel east until the tenth month."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Quanzhong: "The empress is with child; I cannot move east until the tenth month."

sentences.zh: 全忠知帝有謀，遣寇彥卿趣迫。

translations.literal: Quanzhong learned the emperor was plotting and sent Kou Yanqing to press him onward.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw through the emperor's scheme and sent Kou Yanqing to hurry him along.

sentences.zh: 天子不得已，遂行。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had no choice and set out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice and departed.

sentences.zh: 抵谷水，全忠盡殺左右黃門、內園小兒五百人，悉以汴兵為衛。

translations.literal: Reaching Gushui, Quanzhong killed all five hundred eunuchs and inner-palace attendants in the emperor's retinue and replaced them entirely with Bian troops as guards.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushui, Quanzhong slaughtered all five hundred eunuchs and inner-palace attendants around the emperor and replaced every one of them with Bian soldiers as guards.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠至鳳翔，侵邠州，節度使楊崇本降，質其家。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Quanzhong reached Fengxiang and invaded Bin Prefecture, military governor Yang Chongben surrendered and left his family as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Quanzhong marched to Fengxiang and invaded Bin Prefecture, the military governor Yang Chongben surrendered and left his family behind as hostages.

sentences.zh: 崇本妻美，全忠與亂，故崇本怒。

translations.literal: Chongben's wife was beautiful; Quanzhong violated her, so Chongben was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Chongben's wife was beautiful. Quanzhong forced himself on her, and Chongben was furious.

sentences.zh: 至是遣使者會克用、茂貞，南告趙匡凝及建，同舉兵問劫遷狀，全忠大懼。

translations.literal: At this juncture he sent envoys to join Keyong and Maozhen, and southward notified Zhao Kuangning and Jian, calling on them all to raise armies and demand an accounting for the forced removal of the emperor. Quanzhong was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he sent envoys to Keyong and Maozhen and, to the south, alerted Zhao Kuangning and Wang Jian, urging them all to take up arms and demand an explanation for the emperor's abduction. Quanzhong was terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝自出關，畏不測，常默坐流涕。

translations.literal: Since leaving the pass, the emperor feared the unforeseen and often sat silently in tears.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he left the pass, the emperor lived in dread of what might come next and often sat in silence, weeping.

sentences.zh: 玄暉與張廷範內诇，必以告全忠。

translations.literal: Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan spied on him within the palace and always reported to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan kept watch on him inside the palace and always carried word back to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠恨帝無傳禪意，乃謀弒以絕人望，因令其屬李振諭玄暉。

translations.literal: Quanzhong resented that the emperor showed no intention of abdicating in his favor, so he plotted regicide to extinguish popular hope, and had his follower Li Zhen instruct Xuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong hated that the emperor would not abdicate in his favor, so he plotted to kill him and kill off the people's hopes, and sent his man Li Zhen to instruct Xuanhui.

sentences.zh: 玄暉與龍武統軍朱友恭、氏叔琮夜選勇士百人叩行在，言有急奏，請見帝。

translations.literal: Xuanhui with Dragon Martial commander Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong by night selected a hundred brave men and knocked at the traveling palace, saying there was an urgent memorial and requesting to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xuanhui, together with Dragon Martial commander Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong, picked a hundred stalwart men and knocked at the traveling palace, claiming there was an urgent memorial and asking to see the emperor.

sentences.zh: 宮門開，門留十士以守。

translations.literal: The palace gate opened; ten men were left at the gate to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gate opened, and ten men were left behind to hold it.

sentences.zh: 至椒蘭院中，夫人裴貞一啟關，殺之，乃趨殿下。

translations.literal: Reaching the Pepper-Orchid Court, Lady Pei Zhenyi opened the gate and they killed her, then rushed toward the lower hall.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Pepper-Orchid Court, Lady Pei Zhenyi opened the gate and they killed her, then pressed on toward the lower hall.

sentences.zh: 玄暉曰：「上安在？」

translations.literal: Xuanhui said: "Where is His Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui called out, "Where is His Majesty?

sentences.zh: 昭儀季漸榮曰：「院使毋傷宅家，寧殺我！」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Jianrong said: "Commissioner, do not harm the Imperial Household—I would rather you kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Jianrong cried, "Commissioner, do not harm the Son of Heaven—kill me instead!"

sentences.zh: 士持劍入，帝聞，遽單衣走，環柱，遂弒之。

translations.literal: The soldiers entered with swords drawn. Hearing them, the emperor fled in his undergarments, circled a pillar, and was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers burst in with swords drawn. Hearing them, the emperor fled in his underclothes, circled a pillar, and was cut down.

sentences.zh: 漸榮以身蔽帝，亦死。

translations.literal: Jianrong shielded the emperor with her body and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianrong threw her body over the emperor and died as well.

sentences.zh: 復執後，後求哀。

translations.literal: They seized the empress as well; she begged for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the empress too, and she pleaded for her life.

sentences.zh: 玄暉以全忠所弒者帝也，乃釋後。

translations.literal: Xuanhui knew Quanzhong's order was to assassinate the emperor, so he released the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui knew Quanzhong's order had been to kill the emperor alone, so he let the empress go.

sentences.zh: 明日，宰相請對，日晏不出。

translations.literal: The next day the chief ministers requested audience, but as the sun set he had not appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the chief ministers asked for audience, yet the sun was setting and he still had not appeared.

sentences.zh: 玄暉矯遺詔，言帝夜與昭儀博，為貞一、漸榮所弒，出二人首。

translations.literal: Xuanhui forged a death edict saying the emperor had gambled with an attendant-in-ordinary at night and was assassinated by Zhenyi and Jianrong; he produced the two women's heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui forged a death edict claiming the emperor had gambled with an attendant-in-ordinary at night and been murdered by Zhenyi and Jianrong, and he displayed the two women's severed heads.

sentences.zh: 全忠自河中來朝，振曰：「晉文帝殺高貴鄉公，歸罪成濟。

translations.literal: Quanzhong came from Hezhong to court audience. Li Zhen said: "When Jin Wendi killed the Duke of Gaoguixiang, he blamed Cheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong came from Hezhong to attend court. Li Zhen said, "When Jin Wendi killed the Duke of Gaoguixiang, he pinned the crime on Cheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 今宜誅友恭等，解天下謗。」

translations.literal: Now you should execute Yougong and the others to dispel calumny throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should execute Yougong and the rest to quiet slander across the realm.

sentences.zh: 全忠趨西內臨，對嗣天子自言弒逆非本謀，皆友恭等罪，因泣下，請討罪人。

translations.literal: Quanzhong hastened to the Western Inner Palace, faced the successor Son of Heaven, declared himself that regicide had not been his original intent and that the guilt lay with Yougong and the rest, wept, and asked to punish the culprits.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong hurried to the Western Inner Palace, faced the new emperor, declared that regicide had never been his plan and that Yougong and the others were to blame, wept, and asked permission to punish the guilty.

sentences.zh: 是時洛城旱，米鬥直錢六百，軍有掠糴者，都人怨，故因以悅眾，執友恭、叔琮斬之。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang was afflicted by drought; a peck of rice cost six hundred cash. Soldiers were looting grain, and the capital populace was resentful. So, to win public favor, he had Yougong and Shuzong seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was in drought at the time; a peck of rice cost six hundred cash. Soldiers were seizing grain by force, and the people of the capital were furious. To placate them, he had Yougong and Shuzong arrested and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 全忠邀九錫，玄暉自持詔趨汴言之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong pressed for the nine bestowals; Xuanhui himself took the edict and hurried to Bian to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was pressing for the nine bestowals, and Xuanhui himself carried the edict to Bian to make the case.

sentences.zh: 還洛不淹日，全忠矯詔收付有司車裂之，貶為兇逆百姓，焚屍都門外。

translations.literal: He had not been back in Luoyang many days when Quanzhong forged an edict to have him taken by the authorities and torn apart by chariots, degraded to the status of a treacherous commoner, and his corpse burned outside the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of his return to Luoyang, Quanzhong forged an edict ordering his arrest, execution by dismemberment, reduction to the rank of treacherous commoner, and the burning of his corpse outside the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 廷範者，以優人為全忠所愛，扈東遷為禦營使，進金吾衛將軍、河南尹。

translations.literal: As for Tingfan, as an actor he was favored by Quanzhong. Escorting the eastward removal, he became commissioner of the Imperial Camp; he was promoted to general of the Golden Crow Guard and mayor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfan had been an actor whom Quanzhong favored. Escorting the emperor east, he became commissioner of the Imperial Camp, then rose to general of the Golden Crow Guard and mayor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 全忠欲以為太常卿，宰相裴樞持不可，繇是樞罷去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong wished to appoint him Minister of Ceremonies; chief minister Pei Shu objected and would not agree, wherefore Shu was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wanted to make him Minister of Ceremonies, but chief minister Pei Shu refused to agree, and Shu was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 柳璨希旨下詔，責中外不得妄言流品清濁，卒用廷範太常卿。

translations.literal: Liu Can, seeking to please, issued an edict rebuking officials inside and outside the court for rashly discussing ranks as pure or base, and in the end Tingfan was made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, eager to please, issued an edict forbidding officials throughout the court from recklessly debating who was noble and who was base, and Tingfan was finally made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 會天子將郊，以為修樂縣使，又與蘇楷等駁昭宗謚。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was about to conduct the suburban sacrifice, he was made commissioner for ritual music and regalia, and together with Su Kai and others rejected Emperor Zhaozong's posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was preparing the suburban sacrifice, he was made commissioner for ritual music and regalia, and with Su Kai and others he rejected Emperor Zhaozong's posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 全忠恚九錫緩也，王殷譖其與璨等祀天祁延唐祚，及玄暉死、璨誅，即貶廷範萊州司戶參軍，軒於河南市。

translations.literal: Quanzhong resented the delay in granting the nine bestowals; Wang Yin slandered him, saying that he with Can and others had sacrificed to Heaven to pray for prolonging the Tang dynasty. After Xuanhui died and Can was executed, Tingfan was immediately demoted to army staff officer at Laizhou and exposed on a stake in the Henan market.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was angry that the nine bestowals were slow in coming. Wang Yin accused him of joining Can and others in sacrificing to Heaven to prolong the Tang mandate. After Xuanhui was killed and Can executed, Tingfan was at once demoted to army staff officer at Laizhou and paraded on a stake through the Henan market.

sentences.zh: 叔琮亦汴州人，中和末隸感化軍，以騎士奮，性沈壯有膽力。

translations.literal: Shuzong was also a native of Bian Prefecture. At the end of the Zhonghe era he joined the Ganhua army, distinguished himself as a cavalryman, and by nature was taciturn, sturdy, and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong too was from Bian Prefecture. At the end of the Zhonghe era he entered the Ganhua army, made a name as a cavalryman, and was by nature quiet, solid, and fearless.

sentences.zh: 從全忠擊黃巢陳、許間，名右諸將，得為親校。

translations.literal: Following Quanzhong in fighting Huang Chao between Chen and Xu, his fame stood to the right of the other generals, and he became a personal guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with Quanzhong against Huang Chao between Chen and Xu, he ranked among the foremost generals and became one of Quanzhong's personal guard officers.

sentences.zh: 與時溥、朱宣戰，以多累表檢校尚書右仆射，為宿州刺史。

translations.literal: Fighting Shi Pu and Zhu Xuan, through repeated petitions he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and appointed prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns against Shi Pu and Zhu Xuan, repeated memorials on his behalf won him appointment as acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 攻趙匡凝於襄陽，不克。

translations.literal: He attacked Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang but failed to capture the city.

sentences.zh: 又與李克用戰洹水，遷曹州刺史。

translations.literal: He again fought Li Keyong at the Huan River and was transferred to be prefect of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Keyong again at the Huan River and was transferred to prefect of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天復初，拔澤、潞，擊太原，授晉慈觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he captured Ze and Lu, attacked Taiyuan, and was appointed military governor of Jin and Ci.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianfu era he took Ze and Lu, attacked Taiyuan, and was made military governor of Jin and Ci.

sentences.zh: 全忠屯鳳翔，克用襲絳州，攻臨汾，叔琮以二壯士類沙陀者牧馬於原，與克用軍偕行，伺隙各禽一虜還。

translations.literal: While Quanzhong was encamped at Fengxiang, Keyong raided Jiang Prefecture and attacked Linfen. Shuzong sent two stalwart men resembling Shatuo to herd horses on the plain; they traveled alongside Keyong's army, seized an opportunity, and each captured one enemy soldier and returned.
translations.idiomatic: While Quanzhong was encamped at Fengxiang, Keyong raided Jiang Prefecture and attacked Linfen. Shuzong sent two tough men who looked like Shatuo to herd horses on the plain; they marched alongside Keyong's army, waited for an opening, and each seized one enemy soldier and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 克用大驚，疑有伏，遂退屯蒲。

translations.literal: Keyong was greatly alarmed, suspected an ambush, and withdrew to camp at Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was badly shaken, suspected an ambush, and pulled back to camp at Pu.

sentences.zh: 會朱友寧以兵三萬來援，叔琮曰：「賊遁矣，無以立功。」

translations.literal: When Zhu Youning came with thirty thousand troops as reinforcements, Shuzong said: "The enemy has fled—there is no way to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youning arrived with thirty thousand reinforcements, Shuzong said, "The enemy has run off—there is no glory to be won.

sentences.zh: 乃潛師夜獵遊騎，殺數百，進破其壘，俘斬萬級，收馬三千，遂長驅取汾州，轉戰薄太原而還。

translations.literal: So by night he secretly led troops to hunt down roaming cavalry, killed several hundred, advanced and broke their fortified camp, captured and killed enemies by the tens of thousands, collected three thousand horses, then drove deep to seize Fen Prefecture, fought his way close to Taiyuan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: So by night he secretly led troops against roaming cavalry, killed several hundred, broke their fortified camp, took and slew enemies by the tens of thousands, gathered three thousand horses, then drove deep to seize Fen Prefecture, fought his way to the outskirts of Taiyuan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校司空，再進為保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Grand Master and again advanced to military governor of the Baoda army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Grand Master and later to military governor of the Baoda army.

sentences.zh: 全忠欲遷帝於洛，表為右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong wished to move the emperor to Luoyang, he memorialized to appoint Shuzong Right Dragon Martial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong planned to move the emperor to Luoyang, he memorialized to make Shuzong Right Dragon Martial commander.

sentences.zh: 與弒帝，故全忠請貶白州司戶參軍，斬之。

translations.literal: Having joined in assassinating the emperor, Quanzhong requested his demotion to army staff officer at Baizhou and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had helped assassinate the emperor, Quanzhong had him demoted to army staff officer at Baizhou and executed.

sentences.zh: 叔琮將死，呼曰：「朱溫賣我以取容天下，神理謂何？」

translations.literal: Facing death, Shuzong cried out: "Zhu Wen sold me out to win acceptance from the realm—what does divine principle say to that?"
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death, Shuzong cried, "Zhu Wen sold me out to win favor with the world—what does Heaven make of that?"

sentences.zh: 友恭者，本李彥威也。

translations.literal: As for Yougong, his original name was Li Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong's original name was Li Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 壽州人，客汴州。

translations.literal: A native of Shou Prefecture, he had settled in Bian Prefecture as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He was from Shou Prefecture and had lived in Bian Prefecture as a sojourner.

sentences.zh: 殖財任俠，全忠愛而子畜之。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth and practiced knight-errantry; Quanzhong favored him and raised him like a son.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed wealth and lived as a knight-errant; Quanzhong favored him and raised him like a son.

sentences.zh: 領長劍都，積功，表為檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: He commanded the Long Sword division; through accumulated merit he was memorialized as acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Long Sword division, and through accumulated merit was memorialized for appointment as acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，授汝州刺史，檢校司空。

translations.literal: During the Qianning era he was appointed prefect of Ru Prefecture and acting Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning era he was made prefect of Ru Prefecture and acting Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 楊行密侵鄂州，友恭將兵萬餘援杜洪，至江州，還攻黃州，入之，獲行密將，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: When Yang Xingmi invaded E Prefecture, Yougong led more than ten thousand troops to aid Du Hong. Reaching Jiang Prefecture, he turned back to attack Huang Prefecture, entered it, captured Xingmi's generals, and took captives and heads numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi invaded E Prefecture, Yougong led more than ten thousand men to aid Du Hong. At Jiang Prefecture he turned back to attack Huang Prefecture, took the city, captured Xingmi's generals, and killed and captured enemies by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又襲安州，殺守將。

translations.literal: He again raided An Prefecture and killed the defending general.
translations.idiomatic: He raided An Prefecture again and killed the defending general.

sentences.zh: 遷潁州刺史、感化軍節度留後。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ying Prefecture and acting military governor of Ganhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Ying Prefecture and acting military governor of Ganhua.

sentences.zh: 帝東遷，為左龍武統軍，貶崖州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved east, he became Left Dragon Martial commander and was demoted to army staff officer at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east, he became Left Dragon Martial commander, then was demoted to army staff officer at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 臨刑曰：「溫殺我，當亦滅族！」

translations.literal: At execution he said: "When Wen kills me, his clan too shall be destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: At the block he cried, "When Wen kills me, his whole clan will be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 又語張廷範曰：「公行及此」雲。

translations.literal: He also spoke to Zhang Tingfan, saying, "Your turn will come," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He is also said to have told Zhang Tingfan, "Your turn will come."

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：木將壞，蟲實生之；

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】The appraisal says: When a tree is about to decay, vermin breed within it;
translations.idiomatic: 【Appraisal】The appraisal says: When a tree is about to rot, worms hatch inside it;

sentences.zh: 國將亡，妖實產之。

translations.literal: when a state is about to perish, monsters are born from it.
translations.idiomatic: when a state is about to fall, demons are born from it.

sentences.zh: 故三宰嘯兇牝奪辰，林甫將蕃黃屋奔，鬼質敗謀興元蹙，崔、柳倒持李宗覆。

translations.literal: Hence the three chancellors howled like fiends and a woman usurped the celestial hour; Linfu gave command to frontier generals and the imperial carriage fled; Guizhi ruined counsel and Xingyuan was pressed hard; Cui and Liu held the blade reversed and the Li clan was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that three chancellors roared like beasts while a woman seized the hour; Linfu put barbarian generals in command and the emperor fled; Lu Qi wrecked good counsel and the court was driven to Xingyuan; Cui and Liu turned the sword against their master and the house of Li fell.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，有國家者，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Alas—those who hold a state, can they fail to take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—can any who hold a state afford not to take warning!
